title.en: Volume 105 Biographies 30: Zhangsun Wuji and Uncle Chang and Uncle Cao, Son Quan, Young Relative: Shunde, Chu Suilang, Han Yuan, Lai Ji, Li Yiyan's Nephew Yi Chen, Shang Guanyi
title.raw: 卷一百零五 列傳第三十 長孫無忌從父:敞 從父弟:操 子:詮 族叔:順德 褚遂良 韓瑗 來濟 李義琰從祖弟:義琛 上官儀 Volume 105 Biographies 30: Zhangsun Wuji and Uncle Chang and Uncle Cao, Son Quan, Young Relative: Shunde, Chu Suilang, Han Yuan, Lai Ji, Li Yiyan's Nephew Yi Chen, Shang Guanyi

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌從父:敞 從父弟:操 子:詮 族叔:順德 褚遂良曾孫:璆 韓瑗 來濟異母兄:恒 李義琰子:巢 從祖弟:義琛 上官儀

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji paternal uncle by father's brother: Chang; younger paternal uncle by father's brother: Cao; son: Quan; clan uncle: Shunde; Chu Suiliang great-grandson: Qiu; Han Yuan; Lai Ji half-brother by different mother: Heng; Li Yiyan son: Chao; younger cousin by father's brother: Yichen; Shangguan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji; his father's elder brother's son Chang; his father's younger brother Cao; his son Quan; his clan uncle Shunde; Chu Suiliang's great-grandson Qiu; Han Yuan; Lai Ji and his half-brother Heng; Li Yiyan and his son Chao and his cousin Yichen; and Shangguan Yi.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌，字輔機。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji, style name Fujii.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji, whose style name was Fujii.

sentences.zh: 性通悟，博涉書史。

translations.literal: Nature penetrating and quick to understand, broadly traversed books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted by nature and widely read in books and history.

sentences.zh: 始，高祖兵度河，進謁長春宮，授渭北道行軍典簽。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Gaozu's army crossed the river, he advanced to pay respects at Changchun Palace and was appointed military staff officer of the Weibei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu's army first crossed the Yellow River, Wuji went to pay his respects at Changchun Palace and was appointed staff officer on the Weibei campaign.

sentences.zh: 從秦王征討有功，累擢比部郎中、上党縣公。

translations.literal: Following the Prince of Qin on campaigns with merit, repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Justice and Duke of Shangdang County.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Qin on military campaigns with distinction and was promoted in succession to Director in the Ministry of Justice and Duke of Shangdang County.

sentences.zh: 皇太子建成毒王，王病，舉府危駭。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Jiancheng poisoned the prince; the prince fell ill, and the whole household was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Li Jiancheng poisoned the Prince of Qin, who fell gravely ill, throwing the entire household into alarm.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡謂無忌曰：「禍隙已芽，敗不旋踵矣。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling said to Wuji: "The gap of disaster has already sprouted; defeat will come before one can turn the heel.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling said to Wuji, "The seeds of disaster have already been sown; ruin will follow in no time.

sentences.zh: 夫就大計者遺細行，周公所以絀管、蔡也。」

translations.literal: Now, one who pursues the great plan sets aside minor conduct—this is why the Duke of Zhou demoted Guan and Cai."
translations.idiomatic: Those who pursue a great design must set aside petty scruples—this is why the Duke of Zhou punished his brothers Guan and Cai.

sentences.zh: 遂俱入白王，請先事誅之，王未許。

translations.literal: They then both entered to report to the prince, asking to strike first and execute him; the prince did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: They then went in together to inform the prince and urged him to strike first and kill Jiancheng, but the prince would not agree.

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「大王以舜何如人？」

translations.literal: Wuji said: "Great Prince, what sort of man do you take Shun to be?"
translations.idiomatic: Wuji said, "Your Highness, what sort of man do you consider Shun to have been?

sentences.zh: 王曰：「浚哲文明，為子孝，為君仁，又何議哉？」

translations.literal: The prince said: "Deeply wise and civilly brilliant—as a son filial, as a ruler benevolent; what is there to dispute?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince replied, "Deeply wise and civilly brilliant—as a son he was filial, as a ruler he was benevolent. What more is there to say?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「向使浚井弗出，得為孝乎？

translations.literal: He replied: "If he had dug a well and not come out, could he have been filial?
translations.idiomatic: Wuji answered, "If he had been trapped in a well and never come out, could he still have been called filial?

sentences.zh: 塗廩弗下，得為仁乎？

translations.literal: If the granary roof had not been lowered, could he have been benevolent?
translations.idiomatic: If he had not lowered the granary roof, could he still have been called benevolent?

sentences.zh: 大杖避，小杖受，良有以也。」

translations.literal: Avoid the great staff, accept the small staff—there is good reason for this."
translations.idiomatic: Avoid the heavy blow, accept the light one—there is sound reason in that."

sentences.zh: 王未決。

translations.literal: The prince had not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: The prince still could not decide.

sentences.zh: 事益急，乃遣無忌陰召房玄齡、杜如晦定計。

translations.literal: As matters grew more urgent, he sent Wuji secretly to summon Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui to settle the plan.
translations.idiomatic: As the crisis intensified, the prince sent Wuji in secret to summon Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui to finalize their plan.

sentences.zh: 無忌與尉遲敬德、侯君集、張公謹、劉師立、公孫武達、獨孤彥雲、杜君綽、鄭仁恭、李孟嘗討難，平之。

translations.literal: Wuji, together with Yuchi Jingde, Hou Junji, Zhang Gongjin, Liu Shili, Gongsun Wuda, Dugu Yanyun, Du Junchuo, Zheng Rengong, and Li Mengchang, put down the crisis and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji joined Yuchi Jingde, Hou Junji, Zhang Gongjin, Liu Shili, Gongsun Wuda, Dugu Yanyun, Du Junchuo, Zheng Rengong, and Li Mengchang in suppressing the uprising and restoring order.

sentences.zh: 王為皇太子，授左庶子。

translations.literal: When the prince became crown prince, he was appointed Left Guardian of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, Wuji was appointed Left Guardian of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 即位，遷吏部尚書，以功第一，進封齊國公。

translations.literal: Upon accession, he was transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; for merit ranked first, he was advanced to Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince ascended the throne, Wuji was made Minister of Personnel; ranked first in merit, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 帝以無忌皇后兄，又少相友，眷倚日厚，常出入臥內。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Wuji was the empress's elder brother and they had been friends since youth, favored and relied on him daily more deeply, and he often entered and left the sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wuji was the empress's elder brother and had been his friend since youth, the emperor's favor and reliance on him grew daily, and Wuji was often admitted to the inner bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 進尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利可汗已盟而政亂，諸將請遂討之。

translations.literal: The Türkic qaghan Jieli had already sworn alliance but his government was in disorder, and the generals requested to pursue and attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Türkic qaghan Jieli had sworn alliance with the Tang but his realm was in turmoil, and the generals urged an immediate campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 帝顧新歃血，不取為失機，取之失信，計猶豫，以問大臣。

translations.literal: The emperor looked back on the recent blood oath: not taking action would mean losing the opportunity; taking action would mean breaking faith. His plan was hesitant, and he asked the great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reflected on their recent blood oath: to refrain would be to miss the moment, yet to attack would be to break faith. Uncertain, he consulted his senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀曰：「兼弱攻昧，討之便。」

translations.literal: Xiao Yu said: "To combine with the weak and attack the dim—attacking would be convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu said, "It is the way of statecraft to join with the weak and strike the faltering—an attack would be expedient.

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「今我務戢兵，待夷狄至，乃可擊。

translations.literal: Wuji said: "Now we aim to sheathe the sword; wait until the barbarians come, and then we may strike.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji said, "Our present aim is to keep the sword sheathed. Let us wait until the barbarians come to us, and then we may strike.

sentences.zh: 使遂弱，且不能來，我又何求？

translations.literal: If they thus grow weak and moreover cannot come, what more do I seek?
translations.idiomatic: If they weaken and cannot even come, what more do we need?

sentences.zh: 臣謂按甲存信便。」

translations.literal: Your subject considers keeping the armor on and preserving faith to be convenient."
translations.idiomatic: I believe it is better to hold our forces in check and honor our pledge."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 然卒取突厥。

translations.literal: Yet in the end he took the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he did subdue the Türks.

sentences.zh: 或有言無忌權太盛者，帝持表示無忌曰：「我與公君臣間無少疑，使各懷所聞不言，斯則蔽矣。」

translations.literal: Some said Wuji's power was too great; the emperor took a memorial and showed it to Wuji, saying: "Between us lord and minister there is not the slightest doubt. If each keeps what he hears and does not speak, that is blindness."
translations.idiomatic: When some said Wuji's power had grown too great, the emperor showed him the memorial and said, "Between us as ruler and minister there should be no shadow of doubt. If each of you keeps what he hears to himself, that is how courts go blind.

sentences.zh: 因普示君臣曰：「朕子幼，無忌于我有大功，視之猶子也。

translations.literal: He then broadly showed the ministers and said: "My sons are young. Wuji has great merit toward me; I regard him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: He then displayed it to the whole court and declared, "My sons are still young. Wuji has rendered me great service, and I regard him as a son.

sentences.zh: 疏間親、新間舊之謂不順，朕無取焉。」

translations.literal: To estrange the close and set the new against the old is called disloyalty; I will not take it."
translations.idiomatic: To drive wedges between kin and to set newcomers against old companions is disloyalty, and I will have none of it."

sentences.zh: 無忌亦自懼貴且亢，後又數言之，遂解僕射，授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Wuji also feared himself lofty and overbearing; later, when such words were repeated several times, he was relieved of the vice directorship and granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the status of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji himself feared that his rank had grown too high and proud. After such remarks were repeated, he was relieved of the vice directorship and given the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the status of the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 與房玄齡、杜如晦、尉遲敬德皆以元勳封一子郡公。

translations.literal: Together with Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and Yuchi Jingde, each founding merit was enfeoffed with one son as a Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He, together with Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and Yuchi Jingde, was granted a hereditary commandery dukedom for one son each in recognition of their founding merit.

sentences.zh: 進冊司空，知門下、尚書省事，無忌辭，又因高士廉口陳「以外戚位三公，嫌議者謂天子以私後家」。

translations.literal: He was advanced and enfeoffed as Minister of Works, and put in charge of the Chancellery and Department of State Affairs. Wuji declined, and again through Gao Shilian orally stated: "As an affinal kinsman to hold one of the Three Dukes—critics will say the Son of Heaven favors his wife's family by private favor."
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Minister of Works and put in charge of the Chancellery and the Department of State Affairs. Wuji declined, and through Gao Shilian he added that as an imperial in-law occupying one of the Three Ducal posts, critics would say the emperor was favoring his wife's clan.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕任官必以才，不者，雖親若襄邑王神符，不妄授；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I appoint officials necessarily by talent. If not, though as close as Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu, I do not rashly grant office;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "I appoint men solely by talent. Without it, even a kinsman as close as Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu would not receive office rashly;

sentences.zh: 若才，雖仇如魏征，不棄也。

translations.literal: if there is talent, though an enemy like Wei Zheng, I do not discard him.
translations.idiomatic: but where there is talent, even an adversary like Wei Zheng I do not cast aside.

sentences.zh: 夫緣後兄愛昵，厚以子女玉帛，豈不得？

translations.literal: Now, on account of the empress's elder brother's affectionate intimacy, to enrich him with children, jade, and silks—how could that not be permitted?
translations.idiomatic: If I wished merely to shower my empress's brother with honors, wealth, and titles, who could object?

sentences.zh: 以其兼文武兩器，朕故相之，公等孰不曰然？」

translations.literal: Because he combines both civil and military capacity, I therefore made him chief minister—who among you does not say it is so?"
translations.idiomatic: It is because he unites civil and military gifts that I made him chief minister. Do any of you disagree?

sentences.zh: 無忌固讓，詔答曰：「黃帝得力牧，為五帝先；

translations.literal: Wuji firmly declined. An edict replied: "The Yellow Emperor obtained Li Mu and became foremost among the Five Emperors;
translations.idiomatic: Wuji still refused. An edict answered, "The Yellow Emperor had Li Mu and became foremost among the Five Emperors;

sentences.zh: 夏禹得咎繇，為三王祖；

translations.literal: Yu of Xia obtained Gao Yao and became ancestor among the Three Dynasties;
translations.idiomatic: Yu of Xia had Gao Yao and became the ancestor of the Three Dynasties;

sentences.zh: 齊桓得管仲，為五伯長；

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi obtained Guan Zhong and became leader among the Five Hegemons;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi had Guan Zhong and became leader of the Five Hegemons;

sentences.zh: 朕得公，遂定天下。

translations.literal: I obtained you, and thus settled the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I have you, and thus the realm was settled.

sentences.zh: 公其無讓！」

translations.literal: You must not decline!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not decline further!

sentences.zh: 帝又思所與共艱難，賴無忌以免，作《威鳳賦》以賜，且況其功。

translations.literal: The emperor also recalled sharing hardship with him and relying on Wuji to escape danger; he composed "Ode to the Majestic Phoenix" to bestow on him, and moreover praised his merit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also recalled how they had shared hardship together and how he had owed his survival to Wuji. He composed the "Ode to the Majestic Phoenix" as a gift and praised his achievements.

sentences.zh: 帝欲功臣並世襲刺史，貞觀十一年，乃詔有司：「朕憑明靈之祐，賢佐之力，克翦多難，清宇內。

translations.literal: The emperor wished that meritorious ministers should together inherit prefectures in perpetuity. In the eleventh year of Zhenguan, he then issued an edict the relevant offices: "I rely on the aid of bright spirits and the strength of worthy assistants, and have cut down many difficulties and cleared the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to grant his meritorious ministers hereditary prefectures. In the eleventh year of Zhenguan he issued an edict to the relevant offices: "By the aid of bright spirits and worthy assistants, I have overcome many trials and brought order to the realm.

sentences.zh: 蓋時屯共資其力，世安專享其利，朕所不取。

translations.literal: For in times of hardship all shared their strength; in times of peace to enjoy the profit alone—this I do not take.
translations.idiomatic: In hardship all shared their strength; in peace to enjoy the rewards alone is something I will not accept.

sentences.zh: 刺史，古諸侯，雖名不同，而監統一也。

translations.literal: Prefects are the feudal lords of antiquity; though the names differ, their oversight and governance are one.
translations.idiomatic: A prefect is the modern equivalent of the feudal lords of old; the title differs, but the charge of oversight is the same.

sentences.zh: 無忌等義貫休戚，效挺夷險，嘉庸懿績，簡在朕心。

translations.literal: Wuji and the others' righteousness runs through joy and sorrow; their service stands firm through peace and peril; their fine deeds and excellent achievements are selected in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and his fellows have shared my fortunes through good and ill, stood firm in peace and peril, and their fine deeds are engraved on my heart.

sentences.zh: 其改錫土宇，用世及之制。」

translations.literal: Let them be changed and granted domains, using the system of hereditary succession."
translations.idiomatic: Let them be granted domains under a system of hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 乃以無忌為趙州刺史，以趙為公國；

translations.literal: He then made Wuji Prefect of Zhao, with Zhao as his ducal state;
translations.idiomatic: Wuji was made Prefect of Zhao, with Zhao as his ducal domain;

sentences.zh: 房玄齡宋州刺史，國于梁；

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling Prefect of Song, with his state at Liang;
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling Prefect of Song, with his domain at Liang;

sentences.zh: 杜如晦贈密州刺史，國于萊；

translations.literal: Du Ruhui posthumously Prefect of Mi, with his state at Lai;
translations.idiomatic: Du Ruhui, posthumously Prefect of Mi, with his domain at Lai;

sentences.zh: 李靖濮州刺史，國于衛；

translations.literal: Li Jing Prefect of Pu, with his state at Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing Prefect of Pu, with his domain at Wei;

sentences.zh: 高士廉申州刺史，國于申；

translations.literal: Gao Shilian Prefect of Shen, with his state at Shen;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shilian Prefect of Shen, with his domain at Shen;

sentences.zh: 侯君集陳州刺史，國于陳；

translations.literal: Hou Junji Prefect of Chen, with his state at Chen;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji Prefect of Chen, with his domain at Chen;

sentences.zh: 道宗鄂州刺史，王江夏；

translations.literal: Daozong Prefect of E, Prince of Jiangxia;
translations.idiomatic: Daozong Prefect of E, Prince of Jiangxia;

sentences.zh: 孝恭觀州刺史，王河間；

translations.literal: Xiaogong Prefect of Guan, Prince of Hejian;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong Prefect of Guan, Prince of Hejian;

sentences.zh: 尉遲敬德宣州刺史，國于鄂；

translations.literal: Yuchi Jingde Prefect of Xuan, with his state at E;
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jingde Prefect of Xuan, with his domain at E;

sentences.zh: 李勣蘄州刺史，國于英；

translations.literal: Li Ji Prefect of Qi, with his state at Ying;
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji Prefect of Qi, with his domain at Ying;

sentences.zh: 段志玄金州刺史，國于褒；

translations.literal: Duan Zhixuan Prefect of Jin, with his state at Bao;
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhixuan Prefect of Jin, with his domain at Bao;

sentences.zh: 程知節普州刺史，國于盧；

translations.literal: Cheng Zhijie Prefect of Pu, with his state at Lu;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zhijie Prefect of Pu, with his domain at Lu;

sentences.zh: 劉弘基朗州刺史，國于夔；

translations.literal: Liu Hongji Prefect of Lang, with his state at Kui;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hongji Prefect of Lang, with his domain at Kui;

sentences.zh: 張亮澧州刺史，國于鄖。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang Prefect of Li, with his state at Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang Prefect of Li, with his domain at Yun.

sentences.zh: 凡十有四人。

translations.literal: In all there were fourteen men.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen men in all.

sentences.zh: 余官食邑尚不在。

translations.literal: The remaining officials' fief income was not yet included.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining officials' fief incomes were not yet included.

sentences.zh: 無忌等辭曰：「群臣披荊刺，事陛下。

translations.literal: Wuji and the others declined, saying: "Your ministers have braved thorns and brambles in serving Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and the others declined, saying, "We have braved hardship in Your Majesty's service.

sentences.zh: 今四海混一，誠不願違遠左右，而使世牧外州，與遷徙等。」

translations.literal: Now the four seas are united as one; we truly do not wish to be far from Your side and to have generations govern outer prefectures, which would be the same as exile."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the realm is united, we truly do not wish to be sent far from your side to govern distant prefectures in perpetuity, as though we were being exiled.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「割地封功臣，欲公等後嗣長為籓翰，而薄山河之誓，反為怨望，朕亦安可強公土宇邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In carving out land to enfeoff meritorious ministers, I wished that your descendants might long serve as bulwarks of the realm. Yet you slight the oath sworn over mountains and rivers and instead harbor resentment—how can I force domains upon you?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I meant these domains to make your descendants long-term bulwarks of the realm. If you disdain this oath sworn over mountains and rivers and turn resentful instead, how can I force domains upon you?"

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: It was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 後帝幸其第，自家人姻婭勞賜皆有差。

translations.literal: Later the emperor visited his residence; from family members to affinal kin, rewards and gifts were all graded.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor visited his residence and bestowed graded rewards on every member of the household, from kin to in-laws.

sentences.zh: 久之，進位司徒。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was advanced to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾廢，帝欲立晉王，未決，坐兩儀殿，群臣已罷，獨留無忌、玄齡、勣言東宮事，因曰：「我三子一弟，未知所立，吾心亡聊。」

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed, the emperor wished to install the Prince of Jin but had not decided. Seated in the Hall of Two Principles, after the ministers had been dismissed he alone kept Wuji, Xuanling, and Ji to speak of Eastern Palace affairs, and said: "I have three sons and one younger brother; I do not know whom to install. My heart is restless."
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed, the emperor wished to install the Prince of Jin but had not decided. In the Hall of Two Principles, after dismissing the court he kept Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and Li Ji to discuss the succession and said, "I have three sons and one younger brother, and I do not know whom to install. My heart is unsettled.

sentences.zh: 即投床，取佩刀自向，無忌等驚，爭抱持，奪刀授晉王，而請帝所欲立。

translations.literal: He then threw himself on the bed, took his girdle knife and turned it on himself. Wuji and the others were alarmed, rushed to hold him, seized the knife and handed it to the Prince of Jin, and asked whom the emperor wished to install.
translations.idiomatic: He then threw himself on the bed, drew his girdle knife, and turned it on himself. Wuji and the others rushed to restrain him, wrested away the knife and handed it to the Prince of Jin, and asked whom the emperor wished to install.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我欲立晉王。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I wish to install the Prince of Jin."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I wish to install the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「謹奉詔，異議者斬！」

translations.literal: Wuji said: "I respectfully receive the edict. Whoever differs—behead him!"
translations.idiomatic: Wuji said, "Your command is received. Whoever dissents shall be executed!"

sentences.zh: 帝顧王曰：「舅許汝矣，宜即謝。」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to the prince and said: "Your uncle has agreed for you; you should at once give thanks."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to the prince and said, "Your uncle has agreed for you. You should thank him at once."

sentences.zh: 王乃拜。

translations.literal: The prince then bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The prince bowed.

sentences.zh: 帝復曰：「公等與我意合，天下其謂何？」

translations.literal: The emperor again said: "You agree with my intent—what will the realm say?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then said, "You agree with my intent—what will the realm say?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「王以仁孝聞天下久矣，固無異辭；

translations.literal: They answered: "The prince has long been known throughout the realm for benevolence and filial piety; surely there will be no dissent;
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "The prince has long been known throughout the realm for benevolence and filial piety. Surely there will be no dissent;

sentences.zh: 有如不同，臣負陛下百死。」

translations.literal: if there should be any difference, your subject would owe Your Majesty a hundred deaths."
translations.idiomatic: and if there is any dissent, we deserve a hundred deaths before Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 於是遂定。

translations.literal: Thus it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The succession was thus settled.

sentences.zh: 以無忌為太子太師、同中書門下三品，「同三品」自此始。

translations.literal: Wuji was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir and Associate with the Three Departments at the rank of the Three Dukes; "Associate with the Three Dukes" began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir and Associate with the Three Departments at the rank of the Three Dukes—the title "Associate with the Three Dukes" dates from this appointment.

sentences.zh: 帝又欲立吳王恪，無忌密爭止之。

translations.literal: The emperor again wished to install Prince Wu Ke; Wuji secretly remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor again wished to install Prince Wu Ke, Wuji secretly remonstrated and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 帝征高麗，詔攝侍中。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Goguryeo, an edict appointed him acting Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Goguryeo, Wuji was ordered to serve as acting Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 還，辭師傅官，聽罷太子太師，遙領揚州都督。

translations.literal: On return, he resigned the tutor's office; he was permitted to relinquish Grand Preceptor of the Heir and remotely held the post of Military Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's return, Wuji resigned his tutor's post, was relieved of Grand Preceptor of the Heir, and held the distant post of Military Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗從容問曰：「朕聞君聖臣直，人常苦不自知，公宜面攻朕得失。」

translations.literal: The emperor once casually asked: "I have heard that when the ruler is sage the minister is upright, yet people often find it hard to know themselves. You should face me and attack my gains and losses."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked at leisure, "They say that when the ruler is sage the minister is upright, yet men often fail to know themselves. You should speak frankly of my faults and merits.

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「陛下神武聖文，冠卓千古，性與天道，非臣等愚所及，誠不見有所失。」

translations.literal: Wuji said: "Your Majesty is divinely martial and sagely cultured, surpassing all ages; your nature accords with the Way of Heaven—this is not what your foolish ministers can reach. Truly I see no fault."
translations.idiomatic: Wuji replied, "Your Majesty is divinely martial and sagely cultured, surpassing all ages, and your nature accords with Heaven. We are too dull to discern any fault."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕冀聞過，公等乃相諛悅。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I hope to hear of my faults, yet you flatter and please one another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I hoped to hear of my faults, yet you only flatter one another.

sentences.zh: 朕當評公等可否以相規。」

translations.literal: I shall appraise whether each of you is fit and use that to admonish one another."
translations.idiomatic: I shall appraise each of you in turn and use that to admonish you."

sentences.zh: 謂：「高士廉心術警悟，臨難不易節，所乏者骨鯁耳。

translations.literal: He said: "Gao Shilian's mind is alert and perceptive; facing hardship he does not change his integrity—what he lacks is blunt forthrightness.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Gao Shilian is alert of mind and unwavering in crisis—what he lacks is blunt forthrightness.

sentences.zh: 唐儉有辭，善和解人，酒杯流行，發言可意，事朕二十年，未嘗一言國家事。

translations.literal: Tang Jian has eloquence and is good at reconciling people; wine cups circulate, his words are pleasing—yet in twenty years serving me he has never once spoken a word on affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jian is eloquent and skilled at smoothing disputes over wine, and his words are pleasing—but in twenty years of service he has never once spoken on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 楊師道性謹審，自能無過，而懦不更事，緩急非可倚。

translations.literal: Yang Shidao's nature is cautious and careful; he can avoid fault by himself, yet he is timid and inexperienced—in urgent matters he cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shidao is cautious and never errs, but he is timid and inexperienced and cannot be relied on in a crisis.

sentences.zh: 岑文本敦厚，文章、論議其所長也，謀常經遠，自當不負於物。

translations.literal: Cen Wenben is sincere and generous; writing and discourse are his strengths; his plans are always far-reaching—naturally he will not fail the world.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Wenben is sincere and generous; writing and debate are his strengths, and his plans are far-sighted—he will not fail the realm.

sentences.zh: 劉洎堅正，其言有益，不輕然諾於人，能自補闕。

translations.literal: Liu Ji is firm and upright; his words are beneficial; he does not lightly promise others and can himself remedy omissions.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji is firm and upright; his counsel is useful, he does not lightly promise others, and he can remedy his own lapses.

sentences.zh: 馬周敏銳而正，評裁人物，直道而行，所任皆稱朕意。

translations.literal: Ma Zhou is keen and upright; in appraising men he follows the straight path, and in every appointment he has matched my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou is keen and upright; in judging men he follows the straight path, and every man he has recommended has suited my intent.

sentences.zh: 褚遂良鯁亮，有學術，竭誠親於朕，若飛鳥依人，自加憐愛。

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang is blunt and bright, learned in scholarship, devoted and close to me like a bird clinging to a person—I myself add affection for him.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang is blunt and bright, learned, and devoted to me like a bird clinging to its perch—I cannot help but cherish him.

sentences.zh: 無忌應對機敏，善避嫌，求于古人，未有其比；

translations.literal: Wuji is quick and agile in response, good at avoiding suspicion—seeking among men of old, there is none to compare;
translations.idiomatic: Wuji is quick and agile in counsel and skilled at avoiding suspicion—among men of old there is none to compare;

sentences.zh: 總兵攻戰，非所善也。」

translations.literal: commanding troops in attack and battle is not what he excels at."
translations.idiomatic: but commanding troops in battle is not his strength."

sentences.zh: 二十三年，帝疾甚，召入臥內，帝引手捫無忌頤，無忌哭，帝感塞，不得有所言。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the emperor's illness was severe; he summoned Wuji into the sleeping quarters, took his hand and stroked Wuji's jaw; Wuji wept, the emperor was choked with emotion, and could say nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of his reign the emperor fell gravely ill and summoned Wuji to his bedside. He took Wuji's hand and stroked his jaw; Wuji wept, and the emperor, overcome with emotion, could say no more.

sentences.zh: 翌日，與遂良入受詔，顧遂良曰：「我有天下，無忌力也。

translations.literal: The next day, together with Suiliang he entered to receive the edict, and turning to Suiliang said: "I have the realm—this is Wuji's strength.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wuji entered with Suiliang to receive the imperial testament. The emperor turned to Suiliang and said, "I owe this realm to Wuji.

sentences.zh: 爾輔政，勿令讒毀者害之。」

translations.literal: You shall assist in government; do not let slanderers harm him."
translations.idiomatic: Assist in governing, and do not let slanderers destroy him.

sentences.zh: 有頃，崩。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, he passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 方在離宮，皇太子悲慟，無忌曰：「大行以宗廟、社稷屬殿下，宜速即位。」

translations.literal: They were then at a detached palace; the crown prince was grief-stricken. Wuji said: "The late emperor has entrusted the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain to Your Highness; you should quickly ascend the throne."
translations.idiomatic: They were at a detached palace when the crown prince was overcome with grief. Wuji said, "The late emperor has entrusted the ancestral temples and the altars of state to Your Highness. You should ascend the throne at once.

sentences.zh: 因秘不發喪，請還宮。

translations.literal: He therefore kept the death secret and did not announce mourning, requesting to return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the death secret, did not announce mourning, and urged an immediate return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太子即位，是為高宗。

translations.literal: The crown prince ascended the throne; this was Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince ascended the throne and became Emperor Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 進無忌太尉，檢校中書令，猶知門下、尚書二省。

translations.literal: Wuji was advanced to Grand Marshal, acting Director of the Secretariat, and still put in charge of the Chancellery and Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji was promoted to Grand Marshal and acting Director of the Secretariat, while retaining charge of the Chancellery and the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 固辭尚書省，許之。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the Department of State Affairs; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the Department of State Affairs, and his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 帝欲立武昭儀為后，無忌固言不可。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to install Lady Wu Zhaoyi as empress; Wuji firmly said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to install Lady Wu as empress, Wuji firmly declared that it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 帝密以寶器錦帛十余車賜之，又幸其第，擢三子皆朝散大夫，昭儀母復詣其家申請。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly bestowed on him more than ten cartloads of precious vessels and silks, also visited his residence, promoted all three sons to Masters of Palace Attendance, and Lady Zhaoyi's mother again came to his house to plead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly sent him more than ten cartloads of treasures and silks, visited his residence in person, promoted all three of his sons to Masters of Palace Attendance, and Lady Wu's mother came again to plead at his door.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗數勸之，無忌厲色折拒。

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong repeatedly urged him; Wuji sternly refused with a harsh countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong repeatedly urged him on, but Wuji sternly refused.

sentences.zh: 帝后召無忌、遂良及于志寧言后無息，昭儀有子，必欲立之者。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress summoned Wuji, Suiliang, and Yu Zhining, saying the empress had no sons while Lady Zhaoyi had a son, and that they were determined to install her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress summoned Wuji, Suiliang, and Yu Zhining and said that the empress had no sons while Lady Wu had a son, and that they were determined to install her.

sentences.zh: 無忌已數諫，即曰：「先帝付託遂良，願陛下訪之。」

translations.literal: Wuji had already remonstrated several times and then said: "The late emperor entrusted Suiliang; I hope Your Majesty will consult him."
translations.idiomatic: Wuji, having already remonstrated several times, said, "The late emperor entrusted Suiliang. Your Majesty should consult him.

sentences.zh: 遂良極道不可，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Suiliang exhaustively stated it could not be done; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang argued with all his force that it could not be done, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 后既立，以無忌受賜而不助己，銜之。

translations.literal: After the empress was installed, because Wuji had received gifts yet did not assist her, she harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Once Empress Wu was installed, she resented Wuji for accepting imperial gifts yet refusing to support her.

sentences.zh: 敬宗揣后指，陰使洛陽人李奉節上無忌變事，與侍中辛茂將臨按，傅致反狀。

translations.literal: Jingzong divined the empress's intent and secretly had the Luoyang man Li Fengjie report Wuji's treason; together with Palace Attendant Xin Maojiang he would conduct an investigation on the spot and fabricate evidence of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the empress's intent, Jingzong secretly had a Luoyang man named Li Fengjie accuse Wuji of treason, and together with Palace Attendant Xin Maojiang he went to investigate and fabricate a case of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝驚曰：「將妄人構間，殆不其然。」

translations.literal: The emperor was alarmed and said: "Perhaps a reckless man is fabricating discord—probably it is not so."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was alarmed and said, "Surely some reckless man is fabricating discord—it cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 敬宗具言：「反跡已露，陛下不忍，非社稷之福。」

translations.literal: Jingzong fully stated: "The traces of rebellion are already exposed; if Your Majesty cannot bear to act, it is not a blessing to the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong replied in full, "The evidence of rebellion is already plain. If Your Majesty cannot bring yourself to act, it will not be a blessing to the realm."

sentences.zh: 帝泣曰：「我家不幸，高陽公主與我同氣，往謀反，今舅復爾，使我重愧天下，奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said: "My house is unfortunate. Princess Gaoyang shared my blood and once plotted rebellion; now my uncle does the same—how can I again shame the realm? What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said, "My house is cursed. Princess Gaoyang, my own sister, once plotted rebellion; now my uncle does the same. How can I again shame the realm before all the world? What am I to do?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「房遺愛口乳臭，與女子反，安能就事？

translations.literal: He replied: "Fang Yiai still smells of milk on his lips; he rebelled with a woman—how could he accomplish the deed?
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong answered, "Fang Yiai is still wet behind the ears; he rebelled at a woman's instigation—how could he have accomplished anything?

sentences.zh: 無忌奸雄，天下所畏伏，一旦竊發，陛下誰使禦之？

translations.literal: Wuji is a crafty hero whom the realm fears and submits to; if he should secretly rise in revolt one day, whom would Your Majesty send to resist him?
translations.idiomatic: Wuji is a cunning and formidable man whom the realm fears and obeys. If he should rise in secret rebellion, whom would Your Majesty send against him?

sentences.zh: 今即急，恐攘袂一呼，以嘯同惡，且為宗廟憂。

translations.literal: If urgent action is not taken now, I fear he may roll up his sleeves and shout once, gathering fellow evildoers—and the ancestral temples will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not act at once, I fear he may raise his sleeves and summon all who share his evil intent—and the ancestral temples will be in peril.

sentences.zh: 陛下不見隋室乎？

translations.literal: Has Your Majesty not seen the house of Sui?
translations.idiomatic: Has Your Majesty forgotten the house of Sui?

sentences.zh: 宇文化及父宰相，弟尚主，而身掌禁兵，煬帝處之不疑，然而起為戎首，遂亡隋。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji's father was chief minister, his younger brother married an imperial princess, and he himself held the forbidden troops; Emperor Yang treated him without suspicion—yet he rose as leader of the rebels and thus the Sui perished.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Huaji's father had been chief minister, his brother married an imperial princess, and he himself commanded the palace guard. Emperor Yang trusted him completely—yet he rose as leader of the rebels and the Sui was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 願陛下決之。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will decide."
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to decide at once."

sentences.zh: 帝猶疑，更詔審核。

translations.literal: The emperor still doubted and issued another edict for review.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still hesitated and ordered a further investigation.

sentences.zh: 明日，敬宗言無忌反明甚，請逮捕。

translations.literal: The next day Jingzong said Wuji's rebellion was clearly evident and requested arrest.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jingzong declared that Wuji's guilt was clear and requested his arrest.

sentences.zh: 帝泣曰：「舅果爾，我決不忍殺，後世其謂我何？」

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said: "If my uncle is truly so, I absolutely cannot bear to kill him—what will posterity say of me?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said, "If my uncle is truly guilty, I absolutely cannot bring myself to kill him. What will posterity say of me?

sentences.zh: 敬宗曰：「漢文帝舅薄昭，從代來有功，後坐殺人，帝惜撓法，令朝臣喪服就哭之，昭自殺，良史不以為失。

translations.literal: Jingzong said: "Emperor Wen of Han's uncle Bo Zhao came from Dai with merit; later he was convicted of murder. The emperor, loath to bend the law, had court ministers go in mourning dress to weep for him; Zhao killed himself, and good historians do not consider this a fault.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong said, "Emperor Wen of Han's uncle Bo Zhao had served him faithfully since the days in Dai, yet when Bo Zhao was later convicted of murder the emperor, unwilling to bend the law, had court ministers go in mourning dress to weep for him. Bo Zhao killed himself, and good historians do not fault the emperor for this.

sentences.zh: 今無忌忘先帝之德，舍陛下至親，乃欲移社稷、敗宗廟，豈特昭比邪？

translations.literal: Now Wuji forgets the late emperor's virtue, abandons Your Majesty's closest kin, and wishes to shift the altars of state and ruin the ancestral temples—is he to be compared only with Bo Zhao?
translations.idiomatic: Now Wuji has forgotten the late emperor's kindness, abandoned Your Majesty's closest kin, and sought to overturn the altars of state and ruin the ancestral temples—is he to be compared only with Bo Zhao?

sentences.zh: 在法夷五族。

translations.literal: By law his five clans should be exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: By law his five clans should be exterminated.

sentences.zh: 臣聞當斷不斷，反受其亂。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard: when one should decide yet does not, one instead receives disorder.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that he who fails to decide when decision is required invites disaster upon himself.

sentences.zh: 乘機亟行，緩必生變。

translations.literal: Seize the opportunity and act swiftly; delay will surely breed change.
translations.idiomatic: Seize the moment and act swiftly; delay will surely breed disaster.

sentences.zh: 無忌與先帝謀取天下，天下伏其智，王莽、司馬懿之流。

translations.literal: Wuji plotted with the late emperor to seize the realm; the realm submits to his wisdom—he is of the sort of Wang Mang and Sima Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji plotted with the late emperor to win the realm, and the world submits to his cunning—he is of the same breed as Wang Mang and Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 今逆徒自承，何疑而不決？」

translations.literal: Now the rebels themselves confess—why doubt and not decide?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the conspirators themselves have confessed—why hesitate any longer?"

sentences.zh: 帝終不質問。

translations.literal: In the end the emperor did not question Wuji in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the emperor never questioned Wuji in person.

sentences.zh: 遂下詔削官爵封戶，以揚州都督一品俸置於黔州，所在發兵護送；

translations.literal: An edict was then issued stripping his offices, titles, and fief households; he was placed at Qianzhou with the salary of a first-rank Military Governor of Yangzhou, and troops were dispatched along the route to escort him;
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued stripping him of office, title, and fief, placing him at Qianzhou on the salary of a first-rank military governor, with troops dispatched along the route to escort him;

sentences.zh: 流其子秘書監沖等於嶺外；

translations.literal: his son Chong, Director of the Secretariat, and others were exiled beyond the mountain passes;
translations.idiomatic: his son Chong, Director of the Secretariat, and others were exiled beyond the Lingnan passes;

sentences.zh: 從弟渝州刺史知仁貶翼州司馬。

translations.literal: his younger cousin Zhiren, Prefect of Yu, was demoted to Assistant Military Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: his younger cousin Zhiren, Prefect of Yu, was demoted to Assistant Military Governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 後數月，又詔司空勣、中書令敬宗、侍中茂將等覆按反獄。

translations.literal: Several months later, another edict ordered Minister of Works Ji, Director of the Secretariat Jingzong, Palace Attendant Maojiang, and others to reinvestigate the treason case.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later another edict ordered Li Ji, Xu Jingzong, Xin Maojiang, and others to reinvestigate the treason case.

sentences.zh: 敬宗令大理正袁公瑜、御史宋之順等即黔州暴訊。

translations.literal: Jingzong ordered Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Gongyu, Censor Song Zhishun, and others to conduct violent interrogation on the spot at Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong ordered Yuan Gongyu of the Court of Judicial Review and Censor Song Zhishun to conduct violent interrogation at Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 無忌投繯卒，沖免死，殺族子祥，流族弟思于檀口，大抵期親皆謫徙。

translations.literal: Wuji hanged himself with a cord and died; Chong was spared death; clan son Xiang was killed; clan younger brother Si was exiled to Tankou—in general, all close kin were banished and moved.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji hanged himself; Chong was spared death; his clan nephew Xiang was executed; his clan brother Si was exiled to Tankou—in all, his close kin were banished.

sentences.zh: 初，無忌與遂良悉心奉國，以天下安危自任，故永徽之政有貞觀風。

translations.literal: At first Wuji and Suiliang devoted themselves wholeheartedly to serving the state and took the safety and peril of the realm upon themselves; therefore the Yonghui administration had the flavor of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wuji and Suiliang devoted themselves wholeheartedly to the state and took the realm's safety upon themselves, so that the Yonghui era retained something of the Zhenguan spirit.

sentences.zh: 帝亦賓禮老臣，拱己以聽。

translations.literal: The emperor also treated old ministers as honored guests and, with hands folded, listened to them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also honored his senior ministers and listened deferentially to their counsel.

sentences.zh: 綱紀設張，此兩人維持之也。

translations.literal: The laws and institutions were established and displayed—these two men maintained them.
translations.idiomatic: The laws and institutions were upheld—these two men maintained them.

sentences.zh: 既二後廢立計不合，奸臣陰圖，帝暗於聽受，卒，以屠覆，自是政歸武氏，幾至亡國。

translations.literal: Once their plans on the two empresses' deposition and installation did not agree, wicked ministers plotted in secret; the emperor was dark in what he heard and accepted; in the end he was destroyed by slaughter—from then on power passed to the house of Wu, and the state nearly perished.
translations.idiomatic: Once they disagreed over the deposition and installation of empresses, wicked ministers plotted in secret while the emperor listened to the wrong voices. In the end Wuji was destroyed, and from then on power passed to the house of Wu and the state nearly perished.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，追復官爵，以孫元翼襲封。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan, his offices and titles were posthumously restored, and his grandson Yuanyi inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shangyuan his offices and titles were posthumously restored, and his grandson Yuanyi inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 初，無忌自作墓昭陵塋中，至是許還葬。

translations.literal: At first Wuji had himself prepared a tomb within the precinct of Zhaoling; at this time he was permitted to be reburied there.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji had long since prepared his tomb within the precinct of Zhaoling, and now he was permitted to be reburied there.

sentences.zh: 文宗開成三年，詔曰：「每覽國史至太尉無忌事，未嘗不廢卷而歎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng under Emperor Wenzong, an edict said: "Whenever I read the national history and come to the affair of Grand Marshal Wuji, I never fail to put down the scroll and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaicheng, Emperor Wenzong issued an edict saying, "Whenever I read the national history and come to Grand Marshal Wuji's case, I cannot help but put down the scroll and sigh.

sentences.zh: 其以裔孫鈞為猗氏令。」

translations.literal: Let his descendant Jun be made Magistrate of Yishi."
translations.idiomatic: Let his descendant Jun be appointed Magistrate of Yishi."

sentences.zh: 無忌從父敞，字休明。

translations.literal: Wuji’s paternal uncle Chang had the courtesy name Xiuming.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji’s paternal uncle Chang had the courtesy name Xiuming.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝為晉王，敞以庫直從畋驪山，王淩危逐鹿，諫曰：「大王冒垂堂，淫原獸，可乎？」

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang of Sui was Prince of Jin, Chang, as a treasury attendant, followed him hunting at Mount Li. The prince climbed dangerous heights in pursuit of deer, and Chang remonstrated, “Your Highness risks standing beneath a hanging hall and indulges in the beasts of the plain. Can this be right?”
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang of Sui was Prince of Jin, Chang, as a treasury attendant, followed him hunting at Mount Li. The prince climbed dangerous heights in pursuit of deer, and Chang remonstrated, “Your Highness risks standing beneath a hanging hall and indulges in the beasts of the plain. Can this be right?”

sentences.zh: 王遂止。

translations.literal: The prince then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then stopped.

sentences.zh: 即位，頗見識擢。

translations.literal: After he took the throne, Chang was recognized and promoted several times.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne, Chang was recognized and promoted several times.

sentences.zh: 及幸江都，留守禁禦。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Jiangdu, Chang remained behind to guard the palace and prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Jiangdu, Chang remained behind to guard the palace and prohibitions.

sentences.zh: 高祖入關，率子弟謁新豐，授將作少監，出為杞州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the passes, Chang led his sons and younger kinsmen to present themselves at Xinfeng. He was appointed vice director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings and sent out as prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered the passes, Chang led his sons and younger kinsmen to present themselves at Xinfeng. He was appointed vice director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings and sent out as prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，坐受賕免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, he was dismissed for accepting bribes.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan, he was dismissed for accepting bribes.

sentences.zh: 太宗以後屬，歲私給稟，償其費。

translations.literal: Taizong, because Chang was related to the empress, privately supplied him with yearly provisions to meet his expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, because Chang was related to the empress, privately supplied him with yearly provisions to meet his expenses.

sentences.zh: 累封平原郡公。

translations.literal: He was eventually enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒贈幽州都督，諡曰良，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously presented as governor of Youzhou, given the posthumous title Liang, and buried in attendance at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously presented as governor of Youzhou, given the posthumous title Liang, and buried in attendance at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 從父弟 操

translations.literal: Younger paternal uncle by father's brother: Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Younger paternal uncle by father's brother: Cao.

sentences.zh: 從父弟操，字元節。

translations.literal: The younger paternal uncle Cao, style name Yuanjie.
translations.idiomatic: His younger paternal uncle Cao, whose style name was Yuanjie.

sentences.zh: 父覽，為周大司徒、薛國公。

translations.literal: His father Lan was Grand Minister of Education of Zhou and Duke of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lan had been Grand Minister of Education under Northern Zhou and Duke of Xue.

sentences.zh: 操有學術。

translations.literal: Cao had learning and scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: Cao was a learned man.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖辟署相國府金曹參軍。

translations.literal: At first Gaozu summoned and appointed him Army Staff Officer of the Gold Bureau in the Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Gaozu appointed him Army Staff Officer of the Gold Bureau in the Chancellor's Office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檢校虞州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was acting Prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made acting Prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 從秦王征討，常侍旁，與聞秘謀。

translations.literal: Following the Prince of Qin on campaigns, he constantly attended at his side and shared in secret plans.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Qin on campaign, constantly attended at his side, and shared in secret plans.

sentences.zh: 徙陝州，城中無井，人勤於汲，操為釃河溜入城，百姓利安。

translations.literal: Transferred to Shaanzhou, where the city had no wells and people toiled at drawing water, Cao diverted the river into the city by channel, and the people benefited and were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When transferred to Shaanzhou, where the city had no wells and the people toiled at drawing water, Cao channeled the river into the city, to the great benefit of the populace.

sentences.zh: 以母喪解，長老守闕頌遺愛。

translations.literal: He resigned on account of his mother's mourning; elders kept watch at the palace gate praising his lingering kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When he resigned to mourn his mother, elders kept vigil at the palace gate praising his kindness.

sentences.zh: 服除，封樂壽縣男。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Leshou County.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was enfeoffed as Baron of Leshou County.

sentences.zh: 為齊、揚、益三州刺史，課皆最，下詔褒揚。

translations.literal: As Prefect of Qi, Yang, and Yi, his assessments were all top-ranked; an edict praised and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: As Prefect of Qi, Yang, and Yi, his performance ratings were always the highest, and edicts praised him.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，以陝州刺史卒，贈吏部尚書，諡曰安，葬給鼓吹，至虞罷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui he died while Prefect of Shaanzhou; posthumously made Minister of Personnel, posthumous name An; burial was granted musical escort, which ceased at the end of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yonghui he died while serving as Prefect of Shaanzhou. He was posthumously made Minister of Personnel with the posthumous name An, and a musical escort was granted for his burial until mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 子 詮

translations.literal: Son: Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Quan.

sentences.zh: 子詮，尚新城公主。

translations.literal: His son Quan married Princess Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quan married Princess Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 詮女兄為韓瑗妻。

translations.literal: Quan's elder sister by a different mother was Han Yuan's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's elder half-sister was the wife of Han Yuan.

sentences.zh: 無忌得罪，詮流巂州，有司希旨殺之。

translations.literal: When Wuji was condemned, Quan was exiled to Xizhou; the relevant offices, seeking to please, killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuji fell from favor, Quan was exiled to Xizhou and killed by officials eager to please the court.

sentences.zh: 詮有甥趙持滿者，工書，善騎射，力搏虎，走逐馬，而仁厚下士，京師無貴賤愛慕之。

translations.literal: Quan had a nephew Zhao Chiman, skilled at calligraphy, good at mounted archery, able to wrestle tigers by strength, and to run after horses; yet he was benevolent and generous to scholars, and in the capital none, high or low, failed to admire him.
translations.idiomatic: Quan had a nephew named Zhao Chiman who was skilled at calligraphy and mounted archery, strong enough to wrestle tigers and run down horses, yet benevolent and humble toward scholars. In the capital, high and low alike admired him.

sentences.zh: 為涼州長史，嘗逐野馬，射之，矢洞于前，邊人畏伏。

translations.literal: As Chief Administrator of Liangzhou, he once chased wild horses and shot one; the arrow pierced through to the front, and the frontier people feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: As Chief Administrator of Liangzhou, he once chased wild horses and shot one—the arrow passed clean through—and the frontier people feared and submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 詮之貶，許敬宗懼持滿才能仇己，追至京，屬吏訊搒，色不變，曰：「身可殺，辭不可枉！」

translations.literal: When Quan was banished, Xu Jingzong feared Chiman's talent and ability to be his enemy; he was pursued to the capital, handed over to officials for interrogation and beating; his countenance did not change, and he said: "My body may be killed, but my words cannot be twisted!"
translations.idiomatic: When Quan was banished, Xu Jingzong feared Chiman's talent and had him pursued to the capital for interrogation and torture. Chiman's countenance never changed, and he said, "You may kill my body, but you cannot twist my words!

sentences.zh: 吏代為占，死獄中。

translations.literal: The officials wrote the confession for him; he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The officials wrote a confession for him, and he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 族叔 順德

translations.literal: Clan uncle: Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: Clan uncle: Shunde.

sentences.zh: 無忌族叔順德。

translations.literal: Wuji's clan uncle Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji's clan uncle Shunde.

sentences.zh: 順德仕隋為右勳衛，征遼當行，亡命太原，素為高祖親厚。

translations.literal: Shunde served the Sui as Right Merit Guard; when the Liaodong campaign required his service, he fled as an outlaw to Taiyuan and had long been treated with close favor by Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Shunde had served the Sui as a Right Merit Guard. When called up for the Liaodong campaign he fled to Taiyuan, where he had long been treated with favor by Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 太宗將起兵，令與劉弘基募士於外，聲備賊，至數萬人，乃結隊按屯。

translations.literal: When Taizong was about to raise troops, he ordered him together with Liu Hongji to recruit men outside, claiming to prepare against bandits, until they reached tens of thousands; then they formed ranks and encamped.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was about to raise troops, he ordered Shunde and Liu Hongji to recruit men in the countryside, claiming to prepare against bandits, until they numbered in the tens of thousands, then formed ranks and encamped.

sentences.zh: 大將軍府建，授統軍，從平霍邑、臨汾、絳郡有功。

translations.literal: When the Grand General's Office was established, he was appointed Army Commander and followed in pacifying Huoyi, Linfen, and Jiang Commandery with merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand General's Office was established he was appointed Army Commander and distinguished himself in pacifying Huoyi, Linfen, and Jiang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 與劉文靜擊屈突通於潼關，通將奔洛陽，順德跳追桃林，執通以獻，遂定陝縣。

translations.literal: Together with Liu Wenjing he struck Qu Tu Tong at Tong Pass; Tong was about to flee to Luoyang; Shunde leapt in pursuit to Taolin, seized Tong and presented him, and thus settled Shaan County.
translations.idiomatic: With Liu Wenjing he attacked Qu Tu Tong at Tong Pass. When Tong tried to flee to Luoyang, Shunde pursued him to Taolin, captured him, and presented him as a prisoner, thus securing Shaan County.

sentences.zh: 以多進左驍衛大將軍，封薛國公。

translations.literal: For many achievements he was advanced to General of the Left Majestic Tiger Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: For his many achievements he was promoted to General of the Left Majestic Tiger Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Xue.

sentences.zh: 討建成餘黨，食千二百戶，賜宮女，詔宿內省。

translations.literal: In suppressing Jiancheng's remaining faction he received a fief of twelve hundred households, was granted palace women, and was ordered to lodge in the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In suppressing Jiancheng's remaining faction he received a fief of twelve hundred households, was granted palace women, and was ordered to lodge in the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄以受賕為有司劾發，帝曰：「順德元勳外戚，爵隆位厚至矣。

translations.literal: Soon he was impeached and exposed by the relevant offices for accepting bribes. The emperor said: "Shunde is a founding merit and an affinal kinsman; his rank is lofty and his position rich enough already.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was impeached for accepting bribes. The emperor said, "Shunde is a founding merit and an imperial in-law; his rank and position are already as high as they can be.

sentences.zh: 若令觀古今自鑒，有以益國家者，朕當與共府庫，何至以貪冒聞乎？」

translations.literal: If he were made to observe past and present as a mirror and had something to benefit the state, I would share the treasury with him—how did it come to be heard that he was greedy and reckless?"
translations.idiomatic: If he would learn from history and serve the state well, I would share the treasury with him—how did he come to be known for greed?

sentences.zh: 因賜帛數十愧切之。

translations.literal: He then bestowed several tens of bolts of silk to shame and admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: He then bestowed several tens of bolts of silk to shame and admonish him.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿胡演曰：「順德以賂破法，不可赦，奈何又賜之？」

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Hu Yan said: "Shunde broke the law through bribery and cannot be pardoned—why bestow gifts on him again?"
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Hu Yan of the Court of Judicial Review said, "Shunde broke the law through bribery and cannot be pardoned—why bestow gifts on him again?

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「使有恥者，得賜甚於戮；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For one who has shame, receiving a gift is worse than execution;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "For a man of shame, receiving such a gift is worse than execution;

sentences.zh: 如不能，乃禽獸也，殺之何益？」

translations.literal: if he cannot, then he is a beast—what good is killing him?"
translations.idiomatic: but if he cannot feel shame, he is no better than a beast—what good would killing him do?"

sentences.zh: 李孝常謀反，坐與交，削籍為民。

translations.literal: When Li Xiaochang plotted rebellion, he was implicated for association and struck from the registers to become a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiaochang plotted rebellion, Shunde was implicated for associating with him and was struck from the registers to become a commoner.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，帝閱功臣圖，見其像，憐之，遣宇文士及視順德，順德方頹然醉，遂召為澤州刺史，復爵邑。

translations.literal: After more than a year the emperor reviewed the portrait gallery of meritorious ministers, saw his image, and pitied him; he sent Yuwen Shiji to look in on Shunde, who was then drunkenly collapsed; he was then summoned as Prefect of Zezhou and his title and fief were restored.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later the emperor reviewed the portrait gallery of meritorious ministers, saw Shunde's image, and took pity on him. He sent Yuwen Shiji to look in on him and found Shunde drunk and disheveled. Shunde was then recalled as Prefect of Zezhou and his title and fief were restored.

sentences.zh: 順德素少檢，侈放自如，至是折節為政，以嚴明稱。

translations.literal: Shunde had always been little restrained, extravagant and free as he pleased; from this time he restrained himself in governing and was known for severity and clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Shunde had always been unrestrained and extravagant, but from this time he reformed his conduct in office and was known for severity and clarity.

sentences.zh: 先時守長多通餉問，順德繩擿無所容，遂為良吏。

translations.literal: Previously prefects and magistrates often exchanged gifts and inquiries; Shunde prosecuted them without tolerance and thus became a good official.
translations.idiomatic: Previously local officials had freely exchanged gifts and favors; Shunde prosecuted them without mercy and became known as an excellent official.

sentences.zh: 前刺史張長貴、趙士達占部中腴田數十頃，奪之以給貧單。

translations.literal: Former prefects Zhang Changgui and Zhao Shida had occupied several tens of qing of fertile land in the prefecture; he seized it and gave it to poor households.
translations.idiomatic: Former prefects Zhang Changgui and Zhao Shida had seized several tens of qing of fertile land in the prefecture; Shunde confiscated it and gave it to poor households.

sentences.zh: 尋坐累還第。

translations.literal: Soon he was implicated on accumulated charges and returned to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was implicated on accumulated charges and returned to private life.

sentences.zh: 喪息女，感疾甚，帝薄之，謂房玄齡曰：「順德無剛氣，以兒女牽愛至大病，胡足恤？」

translations.literal: He lost a daughter and was deeply stricken with illness; the emperor looked down on this and said to Fang Xuanling: "Shunde has no firm spirit—because of attachment to a daughter he fell gravely ill; why is he worth pity?"
translations.idiomatic: When he lost a daughter and fell gravely ill, the emperor looked down on him and said to Fang Xuanling, "Shunde has no firm spirit—he falls gravely ill over a daughter's death. Why should he be pitied?

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，遣使弔之，贈荊州都督，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: Before long he died; an envoy was sent to offer condolences; he was posthumously made Military Governor of Jingzhou, posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died. The emperor sent an envoy to offer condolences, posthumously made him Military Governor of Jingzhou, and gave him the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十三年，封邳國公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhenguan he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhenguan he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pi.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，加贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: During Yonghui he was additionally posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the status of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui he was additionally posthumously granted the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the status of the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 褚遂良

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang.

sentences.zh: 褚遂良，字登善，通直散騎常侍亮子。

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang, style name Dengshan, son of Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat Chu Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang, whose style name was Dengshan, was the son of Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat Chu Liang.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，為薛舉通事舍人。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye under the Sui he was Attendant of Affairs for Xue Ju.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui dynasty he served Xue Ju as Attendant of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 仁杲平，授秦王府鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Ren'guo was pacified, he was appointed Army Staff Officer of the Armor Bureau in the Prince of Qin's household.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren'guo was pacified he was appointed Army Staff Officer of the Armor Bureau in the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累遷起居郎。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of Daily Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he rose in succession to Attendant of Daily Affairs.

sentences.zh: 博涉文史，工隸楷。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in literature and history, skilled in clerical and regular script.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely versed in literature and history and skilled in clerical and regular script calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗歎曰：「虞世南死，無與論書者！」

translations.literal: Taizong once sighed and said: "Since Yu Shinan died, there is no one with whom to discuss calligraphy!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once sighed and said, "Since Yu Shinan died, there is no one with whom I can discuss calligraphy!

sentences.zh: 魏徵白見遂良，帝令侍書。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng reported and presented Suiliang; the emperor ordered him to attend at writing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng introduced Suiliang to the emperor, who ordered him to attend at calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 帝方博購王羲之故帖，天下爭獻，然莫能質真偽。

translations.literal: The emperor was then broadly purchasing old scrolls of Wang Xizhi; the realm competed to present them, yet none could authenticate true and false.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then avidly collecting old works of Wang Xizhi, and the realm competed to present them, yet none could authenticate them.

sentences.zh: 遂良獨論所出，無舛冒者。

translations.literal: Suiliang alone judged their provenance, and there were none wrongly attributed.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang alone judged their provenance, and never misattributed a single piece.

sentences.zh: 十五年，帝將有事太山，至洛陽，星孛太微，犯郎位。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the emperor was about to perform rites at Mount Tai; arriving at Luoyang, a comet appeared in Supreme Palace Enclosure and encroached on the Official's Seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, as the emperor prepared to perform rites at Mount Tai and arrived at Luoyang, a comet appeared in the Supreme Palace Enclosure and encroached on the Official's Seat.

sentences.zh: 遂良諫曰：「陛下撥亂反正，功超古初，方告成岱宗，而彗輒見，此天意有所未合。

translations.literal: Suiliang remonstrated: "Your Majesty has settled disorder and restored the proper order, with merit surpassing antiquity; just as you are about to announce completion at Mount Dai, a comet suddenly appears—this means Heaven's intent is not yet aligned.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang remonstrated, "Your Majesty has settled disorder and restored proper order, with merit surpassing antiquity. Just as you prepare to announce completion at Mount Tai, a comet suddenly appears—Heaven's intent is not yet aligned.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝行岱禮，優柔者數年，臣愚願加詳慮。」

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han performed the Mount Dai rites only after deliberating for several years; your foolish subject wishes that careful consideration be added."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han deliberated for years before performing the Mount Tai rites. I urge Your Majesty to consider the matter more carefully.

sentences.zh: 帝寤，詔罷封禪。

translations.literal: The emperor awoke to this and issued an edict the cessation of the feng and shan rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took heed and issued an edict canceling the feng and shan rites.

sentences.zh: 遷諫議大夫，兼知起居事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Remonstrance Official and concurrently put in charge of daily affairs records.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Remonstrance Official and concurrently put in charge of the daily affairs records.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿記起居，大抵人君得觀之否？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You record daily affairs—may the ruler generally view them or not?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "You keep the daily affairs records—may the ruler generally view them?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「今之起居，古左右史也，善惡必記，戒人主不為非法，未聞天子自觀史也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Today's daily affairs records are the left and right historians of old; good and evil must be recorded to warn the ruler not to act unlawfully—I have never heard of the Son of Heaven viewing the histories himself."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Today's daily affairs records are the left and right historians of old. Good and evil must be recorded to warn the ruler against unlawful acts. I have never heard of a Son of Heaven viewing the histories himself."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕有不善，卿必記邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If I have faults, will you surely record them?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "If I commit faults, will you surely record them?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「守道不如守官，臣職載筆，君舉必書。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Keeping to the Way is not as good as keeping to one's office; my duty is to carry the brush—the ruler's acts must be written."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Keeping to one's office is more binding than keeping to abstract principle. My duty is to carry the brush—the ruler's every act must be written down."

sentences.zh: 劉洎曰：「使遂良不記，天下之人亦記之矣。」

translations.literal: Liu Ji said: "Even if Suiliang did not record it, the people of the realm would also record it."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji added, "Even if Suiliang did not record it, the people of the realm would."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕行有三：一，監前代成敗，以為元龜，二，進善人，共成政道；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "My conduct has three points: first, to observe the success and failure of former ages as a great mirror; second, to advance good men and together complete the way of governance;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "My conduct rests on three principles: first, to observe the successes and failures of former ages as a great mirror; second, to advance good men and together complete the way of governance;

sentences.zh: 三，斥遠群小，有受讒言。

translations.literal: third, to drive away petty men and not accept slanderous words.
translations.idiomatic: third, to drive away petty men and not accept slanderous words.

sentences.zh: 朕能守而勿失，亦欲史氏不能書吾惡也。」

translations.literal: If I can keep these and not lose them, I also wish that the historians cannot write my evil."
translations.idiomatic: If I can hold to these and not fail, I also wish that the historians will have no evil to write of me."

sentences.zh: 是時，魏王泰禮秩如嫡，群臣未敢諫。

translations.literal: At this time Prince Wei Tai's ritual rank and stipend were like those of the legitimate heir, and the ministers did not dare remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Prince Wei Tai received ritual rank and stipend equal to the legitimate heir, and no minister dared remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 帝從容訪左右曰：「方今何事尤急？」

translations.literal: The emperor casually asked those around him: "What matter today is especially urgent?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor casually asked his attendants, "What matter today is most urgent?

sentences.zh: 岑文本泛言禮義為急，帝以不切，未領可。

translations.literal: Cen Wenben spoke generally that ritual and righteousness were urgent; the emperor considered this inapt and did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Wenben spoke generally of ritual and righteousness as most urgent, but the emperor found this inapt and was not satisfied.

sentences.zh: 遂良曰：「今四方仰德，誰弗率者？

translations.literal: Suiliang said: "Now the four quarters look up to your virtue—who does not follow?
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang said, "The four quarters now look up to your virtue—who does not follow?

sentences.zh: 唯太子、諸王宜有定分。」

translations.literal: Only the crown prince and the princes ought to have fixed ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Only the crown prince and the princes ought to have clearly fixed ranks.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「有是哉！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That is so!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is exactly so!

sentences.zh: 朕年五十，日以衰怠，雖長子守器，而弟、支子尚五十人，心常念焉。

translations.literal: I am fifty years old and daily grow weaker and more weary; though the eldest son holds the vessel, younger brothers and branch sons still number fifty, and my heart constantly thinks of this.
translations.idiomatic: I am fifty years old and grow weaker by the day. Though the eldest son holds the vessel of succession, my younger brothers and branch sons still number fifty, and my heart is constantly troubled by this.

sentences.zh: 自古宗姓無良，則傾敗相仍，公等為我簡賢者保傅之。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, when clansmen were not good, ruin followed in succession; you must select worthy men for me to tutor and protect them.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, when imperial clansmen were not well nurtured, ruin followed in succession. Select worthy men to tutor and protect them for me.

sentences.zh: 夫事人久，情媚熟，則非意自生，其令王府官不得過四考，著為令。」

translations.literal: Now, serving men long, familiarity and flattery grow, and improper intentions arise of themselves; let it be ordered that princely household officials may not serve beyond four performance reviews, and let this be established as a statute."
translations.idiomatic: When men serve princes too long, familiarity breeds flattery and improper intentions arise. Order that princely household officials may not serve beyond four performance reviews, and establish this as a statute."

sentences.zh: 帝嘗怪：「舜造漆器，禹雕其俎，諫者十餘不止，小物何必爾邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor once wondered: "Shun made lacquer vessels, Yu carved his sacrificial stands—more than ten remonstrators would not stop; why must it be so over small things?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once wondered aloud, "Shun made lacquer vessels and Yu carved sacrificial stands—more than ten remonstrators would not cease. Why make such a fuss over small things?"

sentences.zh: 遂良曰：「雕琢害力農，纂繡傷女工，奢靡之始，危亡之漸也。

translations.literal: Suiliang said: "Carving and polishing harm the labor of farming; embroidery injures women's work—this is the beginning of extravagance, the gradual approach of peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang said, "Carving and polishing harm farming, and embroidery injures women's work. This is the beginning of extravagance and the gradual approach of ruin.

sentences.zh: 漆器不止，必金為之，金又不止，必玉為之，故諫者救其源，不使得開。

translations.literal: If lacquer vessels do not stop, they must be made of gold; if gold does not stop, they must be made of jade—therefore remonstrators save the source and do not allow it to open.
translations.idiomatic: If lacquer vessels are not stopped, they will be made of gold; if gold is not stopped, they will be made of jade. Remonstrators therefore cut off the source and do not allow it to open.

sentences.zh: 及夫橫流，則無復事矣。」

translations.literal: Once it flows unchecked, there is nothing more to be done."
translations.idiomatic: Once the flood runs unchecked, nothing more can be done."

sentences.zh: 帝咨美之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and commended this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and commended this.

sentences.zh: 于時皇子雖幼，皆外任都督、刺史，遂良諫曰：「昔二漢以郡國參治，雜用周制。

translations.literal: At this time, though the princes were young, all were assigned outside as military governors and prefects. Suiliang remonstrated: "Formerly the two Han dynasties governed through commanderies and kingdoms together, mixing in Zhou institutions.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, though the princes were still young, all were assigned as military governors and prefects in the provinces. Suiliang remonstrated, "The two Han dynasties governed through commanderies and kingdoms together, mixing in Zhou institutions.

sentences.zh: 今州縣率仿秦法，而皇子孺年並任刺史，陛下誠以至親扞四方。

translations.literal: Now prefectures and counties generally follow Qin law, yet princes in tender years are all appointed prefects—Your Majesty truly uses closest kin to defend the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Now prefectures and counties follow Qin-style administration, yet princes still in tender years are all appointed prefects. Your Majesty truly means to use closest kin to defend the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 雖然，刺史，民之師帥也，得人則下安措，失人則家勞攰。

translations.literal: Even so, a prefect is the teacher and leader of the people; with the right man the lower ranks are settled, with the wrong man households are worn and weary.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, a prefect is the teacher and leader of the people. With the right man the people are at ease; with the wrong man households are worn to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 故漢宣帝曰：'與我共治，惟良二千石乎。

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Xuan of Han said: 'Those who govern with me—are they not the good two-thousand-bushel officials?'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Emperor Xuan of Han said, 'Those who govern with me—are they not the good two-thousand-bushel officials?'

sentences.zh: '臣謂皇子未冠者，可且留京師，教以經學，畏仰天威，不敢犯禁，養成德器，審堪臨州，然後敦遣。

translations.literal: Your subject says that princes who have not yet come of age may for the time being remain in the capital, be taught the classics, revere and look up to Heaven's majesty, dare not violate prohibitions, be nurtured into virtue and capacity, and once truly fit to govern a prefecture, then be earnestly dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: I say that princes who have not yet come of age should remain in the capital for the time being, be taught the classics, revere the imperial majesty, and dare not violate prohibitions. Once nurtured into virtue and capacity and truly fit to govern a prefecture, they may then be dispatched.
