sentences.zh: 昔東漢明、章諸帝，友愛子弟，雖各有國，幼者率留京師，訓飭以禮。

translations.literal: Formerly the emperors Ming and Zhang of Eastern Han loved and cared for their younger kinsmen; though each had a state, the young generally remained in the capital and were trained and admonished with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperors Ming and Zhang of Eastern Han loved their younger kinsmen. Though each prince had a state, the young generally remained in the capital and were trained in ritual.

sentences.zh: 訖其世，諸王數十百，惟二人以惡敗，自餘餐和染教，皆為善良。

translations.literal: Through their age the princes numbered in the tens and hundreds; only two were ruined through evil—the rest, nourished by harmony and dyed by teaching, all became good.
translations.idiomatic: Through their reigns the princes numbered in the tens and hundreds, yet only two were ruined through evil. The rest, nourished by harmony and shaped by teaching, all became good men.

sentences.zh: 此前事已驗，惟陛下省察。」

translations.literal: This matter of former ages has already been verified; I hope Your Majesty will examine it."
translations.idiomatic: This precedent has already been tested. I urge Your Majesty to consider it.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted this.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾廢，魏王泰間侍，帝許立為嗣，因謂大臣曰：「泰昨自投我懷中云：『臣今日始得為陛下子，更生之日也。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed, Prince Wei Tai attended at intervals; the emperor agreed to install him as heir and therefore said to the ministers: "Tai yesterday threw himself into my arms and said: 'Today I have finally become Your Majesty's son—it is a day of rebirth.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed, Prince Wei Tai attended the emperor closely, and the emperor agreed to install him as heir. He told the ministers, "Tai yesterday threw himself into my arms and said, 'Today I have finally become Your Majesty's son—it is a day of rebirth.

sentences.zh: 臣惟有一子，百年後，當殺之，傳國晉王。』

translations.literal: Your subject has only one son; after a hundred years, I shall kill him and pass the realm to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: I have only one son; when I die, I shall kill him and pass the realm to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 朕甚憐之。」

translations.literal: I deeply pity him."
translations.idiomatic: I deeply pity him.'

sentences.zh: 遂良曰：「陛下失言。

translations.literal: Suiliang said: "Your Majesty misspoke.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang said, "Your Majesty misspoke.

sentences.zh: 安有為天下主而殺其愛子，授國晉王乎？

translations.literal: How can there be one who is lord of the realm yet kills his beloved son and gives the realm to the Prince of Jin?
translations.idiomatic: How can a lord of the realm kill his beloved son and give the realm to the Prince of Jin?

sentences.zh: 陛下昔以承乾為嗣，復寵愛泰，嫡庶不明，紛紛至今。

translations.literal: Your Majesty formerly made Chengqian heir, then again favored and loved Tai—the legitimate and secondary were unclear, and confusion has continued to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty formerly made Chengqian heir, then again favored Tai—the line between legitimate and secondary heir was never clear, and confusion has continued to the present.

sentences.zh: 若必立泰，非別置晉王不可。」

translations.literal: If Tai must be installed, the Prince of Jin cannot but be set apart elsewhere."
translations.idiomatic: If Tai must be installed, the Prince of Jin must be set apart elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 帝泣曰：「我不能。」

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said: "I cannot."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said, "I cannot."

sentences.zh: 即詔長孫無忌、房玄齡、李勣與遂良等定策立晉王為皇太子。

translations.literal: He then issued an edict Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Li Ji, Suiliang, and others to settle the plan and install the Prince of Jin as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Li Ji, Suiliang, and others to settle the succession and install the Prince of Jin as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時飛雉數集宮中，帝問：「是何祥也？」

translations.literal: At this time flying pheasants repeatedly gathered in the palace; the emperor asked: "What omen is this?"
translations.idiomatic: At this time flying pheasants repeatedly gathered in the palace, and the emperor asked, "What omen is this?

sentences.zh: 遂良曰：「昔秦文公時，有侲子化為雉，雌鳴陳倉，雄鳴南陽。

translations.literal: Suiliang said: "Formerly in the time of Duke Wen of Qin, a boy transformed into a pheasant; the female cried at Chencang, the male at Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang said, "In the time of Duke Wen of Qin, a boy transformed into a pheasant. The female cried at Chencang and the male at Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 侲子曰：『得雄者王，得雌者霸。』

translations.literal: The boy said: 'He who obtains the male shall become king; he who obtains the female shall become hegemon.'
translations.idiomatic: The boy said, 'He who obtains the male shall become king; he who obtains the female shall become hegemon.'

sentences.zh: 文公遂雄諸侯，始為寶雞祠。

translations.literal: Duke Wen then dominated the feudal lords and first established the shrine at Baoji.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen then dominated the feudal lords and first established the shrine at Baoji.

sentences.zh: 漢光武得其雄，起南陽，有四海。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu of Han obtained the male, rose from Nanyang, and possessed the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu of Han obtained the male, rose from Nanyang, and won the four seas.

sentences.zh: 陛下本封秦，故雄雌並見，以告明德。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty was originally enfeoffed in Qin; therefore male and female both appear, announcing bright virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty was originally enfeoffed in Qin; therefore both male and female appear, announcing your bright virtue."

sentences.zh: 帝悅，曰：「人之立身，不可以無學。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and said: "In establishing oneself as a person, one cannot be without learning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and said, "In establishing oneself, one cannot be without learning.

sentences.zh: 遂良所謂多識君子哉！」

translations.literal: Suiliang is what is called a widely learned gentleman!"
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang is truly a widely learned gentleman!"

sentences.zh: 俄授太子賓客。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Guest of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed Guest of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀請婚，帝己納其聘，復絕之。

translations.literal: Xueyantuo requested marriage; the emperor had already accepted their betrothal gifts, then broke it off.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyantuo requested a marriage alliance. The emperor had already accepted their betrothal gifts, then broke off the engagement.

sentences.zh: 遂良曰：「信為萬事本，百姓所歸。

translations.literal: Suiliang said: "Faith is the root of all things and what the people turn to.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang said, "Faith is the root of all things and what the people turn to.

sentences.zh: 故文王許枯骨而不違，仲尼去食存信，貴之也。

translations.literal: Therefore King Wen kept his promise even to dry bones and did not violate it; Confucius said to abandon food but preserve faith—such is its value.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen kept his promise even to dry bones; Confucius said to abandon food but preserve faith—such is its value.

sentences.zh: 延陀，曩一俟斤耳。

translations.literal: Xueyantuo was formerly but one yilijin.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyantuo was formerly but a minor chieftain.

sentences.zh: 因天兵北討，蕩平沙塞，威加諸外，而恩結於內，以為餘寇不可以無酋長，故璽書鼓纛，立為可汗。

translations.literal: Because the heavenly army marched north to attack and swept clear the desert passes, its might extended to all outer lands while grace bound the inner, thinking that remaining bandits could not be without a chieftain—therefore with imperial edict, drums, and banners he was installed as qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army marched north and swept clear the desert passes, its might extended beyond the borders while grace bound the inner tribes. Thinking that the remaining bandits needed a chieftain, the court issued an imperial edict with drums and banners and installed him as qaghan.

sentences.zh: 負抱之恩，與天無極。

translations.literal: The grace of carrying and embracing him is boundless as Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The grace shown him is boundless as Heaven.

sentences.zh: 數遣使請婚于朝，陛下既開許，為禦北門受獻食。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent envoys requesting marriage at court; Your Majesty had already openly promised, and he came to the Northern Gate to present tribute food.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly sent envoys requesting marriage at court. Your Majesty had already openly promised, and he came to the Northern Gate to present tribute food.

sentences.zh: 今一朝自為進退，所惜少，所失多，虧信夷狄，方生嫌恨，殆不可以訓戎兵、勵軍事也。

translations.literal: Now in one morning to advance and retreat by one's own will—what is spared is little, what is lost is much; faith is impaired before the barbarians, resentment is just arising—this can scarcely be used to instruct frontier troops and encourage military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Now to advance and retreat at a whim in a single morning—what is spared is little and what is lost is great. Faith is impaired before the barbarians, resentment is just arising, and this can scarcely instruct frontier troops or encourage military affairs.

sentences.zh: 且龍沙以北，部落牛毛，中國擊之不能盡，亦猶可北敗，芮芮興，突厥亡，延陀盛。

translations.literal: Moreover, north of Longsha the tribes are as numerous as cattle hair; China cannot strike them all down. Just as defeat may come from the north, so Rouran may rise, the Türks perish, and Xueyantuo flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, north of Longsha the tribes are as numerous as cattle hair, and China cannot strike them all down. Just as defeat may come from the north, so Rouran may rise, the Türks perish, and Xueyantuo flourish.

sentences.zh: 是以古人虛外實內，懷之以德。

translations.literal: Therefore the men of old made the outer empty and the inner solid, embracing them with virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the men of old kept the outer realm light and the inner realm strong, embracing the barbarians with virtue.

sentences.zh: 使為惡，在夷不在華；

translations.literal: If evil is done, let it be among the barbarians and not among the Chinese;
translations.idiomatic: If evil is done, let it be among the barbarians and not among the Chinese;

sentences.zh: 失信，在彼不在此也。

translations.literal: if faith is broken, let it be on their side and not on this side.
translations.idiomatic: if faith is broken, let it be on their side and not on ours.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下裁幸。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will judge and decide."
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to judge and decide.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: This was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept this.

sentences.zh: 帝欲自討遼東，遂良固勸無行：「一不勝，師必再興；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to campaign personally against Liaodong; Suiliang firmly urged against going: "One defeat, and the army must be raised again;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to campaign personally against Liaodong, Suiliang firmly urged against it: "One defeat, and the army must be raised again;

sentences.zh: 再興，為忿兵。

translations.literal: raised again, it becomes an army of wrath.
translations.idiomatic: raised again, it becomes an army driven by wrath.

sentences.zh: 兵忿者，勝負不可必。」

translations.literal: An army of wrath—victory and defeat cannot be assured."
translations.idiomatic: An army driven by wrath—victory and defeat cannot be assured.

sentences.zh: 帝然可。

translations.literal: The emperor assented that this was so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed that this was so.

sentences.zh: 會李勣詆其計，帝意遂決東。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Ji slandered his plan, and the emperor's intent was then fixed on the east.
translations.idiomatic: But then Li Ji disparaged his plan, and the emperor's mind was fixed on the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 遂良懼，上言：「臣請譬諸身。

translations.literal: Suiliang feared this and submitted a memorial: "Your subject asks to compare this to the body.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Suiliang submitted a memorial: "I ask to compare this to the body.

sentences.zh: 兩京，腹心也；

translations.literal: The two capitals are the heart and belly;
translations.idiomatic: The two capitals are the heart and belly;

sentences.zh: 四境，手足也；

translations.literal: the four borders are the hands and feet;
translations.idiomatic: the four borders are the hands and feet;

sentences.zh: 殊裔絕域，殆非支體所屬。

translations.literal: remote alien lands at the ends of the earth are scarcely parts of the limbs.
translations.idiomatic: remote alien lands at the ends of the earth are scarcely parts of the limbs at all.

sentences.zh: 高麗王陛下所立，莫離支殺之。

translations.literal: The king of Goguryeo was installed by Your Majesty; Yeon Gaesomun killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Goguryeo was installed by Your Majesty, and Yeon Gaesomun killed him.

sentences.zh: 討其逆，夷其地，固不可失，但遣一二慎將，付銳兵十萬，翔旝雲輣，唾手可取。

translations.literal: To punish his rebellion and level his land cannot be missed, but send one or two careful generals with a hundred thousand sharp troops—soaring banners and cloud chariots—and it can be taken as easily as spitting.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing his rebellion and leveling his land cannot be neglected, but send one or two careful generals with a hundred thousand elite troops under soaring banners and cloud chariots, and it can be taken as easily as spitting.

sentences.zh: 昔侯君集、李靖皆庸人爾，猶能撅高昌，纓突厥，陛下止發蹤指示，得歸功聖明。

translations.literal: Formerly Hou Junji and Li Jing were both ordinary men, yet they could overthrow Gaochang and bind the Türks; Your Majesty need only release the hounds and point the way, and the merit returns to your sage brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Hou Junji and Li Jing were ordinary men, yet they overthrew Gaochang and bound the Türks. Your Majesty need only give the signal and point the way, and the merit returns to your sage brilliance.

sentences.zh: 前日從陛下平天下，虓士爪臣，氣力未衰，可驅策，惟陛下所使。

translations.literal: In former days they followed Your Majesty to pacify the realm—fierce warriors and taloned ministers whose strength is not yet decayed; they can be driven and commanded as Your Majesty wishes.
translations.idiomatic: The fierce warriors and loyal ministers who followed Your Majesty to pacify the realm still have strength undiminished. They can be commanded as Your Majesty wishes.

sentences.zh: 臣聞涉遼而左，或水潦，平地淖三尺，帶方、玄菟，海壤荒漫，決非萬乘六師所宜行。」

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that crossing the Liao and turning left, there are sometimes floods, with three feet of mud on level ground; Daifang and Xuantu are coastal wastelands, vast and desolate—decidedly not where the emperor's six armies ought to march."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that east of the Liao there are floods, with three feet of mud on level ground, and that Daifang and Xuantu are coastal wastelands vast and desolate—decidedly not where the emperor's six armies ought to march.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝銳意蕩平，不見省。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor was keen to sweep and pacify and did not heed this.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor was set on total conquest and did not heed this.

sentences.zh: 進黃門侍郎，參綜朝政。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and participated in comprehensive governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and participated in governing affairs.

sentences.zh: 莫離支遣使貢金，遂良曰：「古者討殺君之罪，不受其賂。

translations.literal: Yeon Gaesomun sent envoys presenting gold tribute; Suiliang said: "In antiquity, when punishing the crime of regicide, one did not accept bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yeon Gaesomun sent envoys presenting gold tribute. Suiliang said, "In antiquity, when punishing regicide, one did not accept bribes.

sentences.zh: 魯納郜鼎太廟，《春秋》譏之。

translations.literal: Lu accepted the tripod of Zou into the Grand Temple—the Spring and Autumn Annals rebuked this.
translations.idiomatic: Lu accepted the tripod of Zou into the Grand Temple, and the Spring and Autumn Annals rebuked this.

sentences.zh: 今莫離支所貢不臣之篚，不容受。」

translations.literal: Now the tribute basket Yeon Gaesomun presents is that of a disloyal subject—it cannot be accepted."
translations.idiomatic: The tribute Yeon Gaesomun presents is that of a disloyal subject and cannot be accepted.

sentences.zh: 詔可，以其使屬吏。

translations.literal: An edict approved this, and his envoys were handed over to officials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved this, and his envoys were handed over to the officials.

sentences.zh: 帝既平高昌，歲調兵千人往屯，遂良誦諍不可，帝志取西域，寘其言不用。

translations.literal: After the emperor had pacified Gaochang, a thousand troops were levied each year to garrison there; Suiliang remonstrated repeatedly that this could not be done; the emperor's intent was to take the Western Regions, and he set aside these words and did not use them.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor pacified Gaochang, a thousand troops were levied each year to garrison there. Suiliang remonstrated repeatedly against this, but the emperor's intent was to take the Western Regions and he ignored the advice.

sentences.zh: 西突厥寇西州，帝曰：「往魏徵、褚遂良勸我立麹文泰子弟，不用其計，乃今悔之。」

translations.literal: The Western Türks raided Xizhou; the emperor said: "Formerly Wei Zheng and Chu Suiliang urged me to install Qu Wentai's sons and younger kinsmen; I did not use their plan, and now I regret it."
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Türks raided Xizhou, the emperor said, "Formerly Wei Zheng and Chu Suiliang urged me to install Qu Wentai's sons and younger kinsmen. I did not use their plan, and now I regret it.

sentences.zh: 帝于寢宮側別置院居太子，遂良諫，以為「朋友深交者易怨，父子滯愛者多愆。

translations.literal: The emperor set up a separate courtyard beside the sleeping palace for the crown prince to dwell; Suiliang remonstrated, saying: "Close friends who associate deeply easily grow resentful; father and son who linger in affection often accumulate faults.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set up a separate courtyard beside the sleeping palace for the crown prince. Suiliang remonstrated, saying, "Close friends who associate too deeply easily grow resentful; father and son who linger too long in affection often accumulate faults.

sentences.zh: 宜許太子間還東宮，近師傅，專學藝，以廣懿德。」

translations.literal: The crown prince should be allowed from time to time to return to the Eastern Palace, be near his tutors, and devote himself to learning and arts to broaden his fine virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince should be allowed to return periodically to the Eastern Palace, be near his tutors, and devote himself to learning so as to broaden his virtue."

sentences.zh: 帝從其言。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 會父喪免，起復，拜中書令。

translations.literal: It happened that he was relieved on account of his father's mourning; he was recalled from mourning and appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he resigned to mourn, but was recalled from mourning and appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝寢疾，召遂良、長孫無忌曰：「歎武帝寄霍光，劉備托諸葛亮，朕今委卿矣。

translations.literal: The emperor lay ill in bed and summoned Suiliang and Zhangsun Wuji, saying: "I sigh that Emperor Wu entrusted Huo Guang, and Liu Bei entrusted Zhuge Liang—I now entrust you.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor lay gravely ill, he summoned Suiliang and Zhangsun Wuji and said, "Emperor Wu entrusted Huo Guang, and Liu Bei entrusted Zhuge Liang—I now entrust you.

sentences.zh: 太子仁孝，其盡誠輔之。」

translations.literal: The crown prince is benevolent and filial; devote yourselves fully to assisting him."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is benevolent and filial. Devote yourselves fully to assisting him.

sentences.zh: 謂太子曰：「無忌、遂良在，而毋憂。」

translations.literal: He said to the crown prince: "With Wuji and Suiliang present, you need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: He told the crown prince, "With Wuji and Suiliang present, you need not worry."

sentences.zh: 因命遂良草詔。

translations.literal: He then ordered Suiliang to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Suiliang to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，封河南縣公，進郡公。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Henan County and advanced to Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended the throne, Suiliang was enfeoffed as Duke of Henan County and then advanced to Duke of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 坐事出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: On account of an offense he was sent out as Prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On account of an offense he was sent out as Prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 再歲，召拜吏部尚書、同中書門下三品，監修國史，兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: After two years he was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, Associate with the Three Departments at the rank of the Three Dukes, Supervisor of the compilation of the national history, and concurrently Guest of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was recalled as Minister of Personnel, Associate with the Three Departments at the rank of the Three Dukes, Supervisor of the national history, and Guest of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 進拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was advanced and appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝將立武昭儀，召長孫無忌、李勣、于志寧及遂良人。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to install Lady Wu Zhaoyi and summoned Zhangsun Wuji, Li Ji, Yu Zhining, and Suiliang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to install Lady Wu as empress, he summoned Zhangsun Wuji, Li Ji, Yu Zhining, and Suiliang.

sentences.zh: 或謂無忌當先諫，遂良曰：「太尉，國元舅，有不如意，使上有棄親之譏。」

translations.literal: Some said Wuji ought to remonstrate first; Suiliang said: "The Grand Marshal is the state's chief maternal uncle; if things go against his wish, it will give the emperor the reproach of abandoning kin."
translations.idiomatic: Some said Wuji ought to remonstrate first. Suiliang said, "The Grand Marshal is the state's chief maternal uncle. If things go against his wish, the emperor will be reproached for abandoning kin.

sentences.zh: 又謂勣上所重，當進，曰：「不可。

translations.literal: They also said Ji was highly valued by the emperor and ought to speak up; he said: "That cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: They also said Li Ji was highly valued by the emperor and ought to speak up. Suiliang said, "That cannot be.

sentences.zh: 司空，國元勳，有不如意，使上有斥功臣之嫌。」

translations.literal: The Minister of Works is the state's chief founding merit; if things go against his wish, it will give the emperor the suspicion of rejecting meritorious ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works is the state's chief founding merit. If things go against his wish, the emperor will be suspected of rejecting his meritorious ministers."

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾奉遺詔，若不盡愚，無以下見先帝。」

translations.literal: He said: "I received the testamentary edict; if I do not exhaust my foolish counsel, I cannot face the late emperor below."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I received the testamentary edict. If I do not exhaust my counsel, I cannot face the late emperor in the afterlife."

sentences.zh: 既入，帝曰：「罪莫大於絕嗣，皇后無子，今欲立昭儀，謂何？」

translations.literal: After entering, the emperor said: "No crime is greater than cutting off the succession; the empress has no son, and now I wish to install Lady Zhaoyi—what do you say?"
translations.idiomatic: After they entered, the emperor said, "No crime is greater than cutting off the succession. The empress has no son, and now I wish to install Lady Wu—what do you say?"

sentences.zh: 遂良曰：「皇后本名家，奉事先帝。

translations.literal: Suiliang said: "The empress is originally from an eminent clan and served the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang said, "The empress is from an eminent clan and served the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 先帝疾，執陛下手語臣曰：『我兒與婦今付卿！』

translations.literal: When the late emperor was ill, he took Your Majesty's hand and spoke to me, saying: 'My son and daughter-in-law I now entrust to you!'
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor was ill, he took Your Majesty's hand and told me, 'My son and daughter-in-law I now entrust to you!'

sentences.zh: 且德音在陛下耳，可遽忘之？

translations.literal: Moreover his virtuous words are still in Your Majesty's ears—how can they be suddenly forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: His virtuous words are still in Your Majesty's ears—how can they be suddenly forgotten?

sentences.zh: 皇后無它過，不可廢。」

translations.literal: The empress has no other fault and cannot be deposed."
translations.idiomatic: The empress has no other fault and cannot be deposed."

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 翌日，復言，對曰：「陛下必欲改立后者，請更擇貴姓。

translations.literal: The next day he spoke again; Suiliang replied: "If Your Majesty must change and install a new empress, please choose another from an eminent clan.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Suiliang spoke again and said, "If Your Majesty must install a new empress, please choose another from an eminent clan.

sentences.zh: 昭儀昔事先帝，身接帷第，今立之，奈天下耳目何？」

translations.literal: Lady Zhaoyi formerly served the late emperor and shared his bedchamber; to install her now—what of the eyes and ears of the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu formerly served the late emperor and shared his bedchamber. To install her now—what will the eyes and ears of the realm say?

sentences.zh: 帝羞默。

translations.literal: The emperor was ashamed and silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was ashamed and fell silent.

sentences.zh: 遂良因致笏殿階，叩頭流血，曰：「還陛下此笏，丐歸田里。」

translations.literal: Suiliang therefore placed his tablet on the palace steps, knocked his head until it bled, and said: "I return this tablet to Your Majesty and beg to go home to my fields."
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang placed his court tablet on the palace steps, kowtowed until it bled, and said, "I return this tablet to Your Majesty and beg to retire to my fields.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，命引出。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered him led out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered him led out.

sentences.zh: 武氏從幄後呼曰：「何不撲殺此獠？」

translations.literal: Lady Wu called from behind the curtain: "Why not beat this brute to death?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu called from behind the curtain, "Why not beat this brute to death?

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「遂良受顧命，有罪不加刑。」

translations.literal: Wuji said: "Suiliang received the testamentary charge; though guilty, he shall not be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Wuji said, "Suiliang received the testamentary charge. Even if guilty, he shall not be punished."

sentences.zh: 會李勣議異，武氏立，乃左遷遂良潭州都督。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Ji's opinion differed; Lady Wu was installed, and Suiliang was demoted and transferred as Military Governor of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji's opinion differed, Lady Wu was installed, and Suiliang was demoted to Military Governor of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，徙桂州，未幾，貶愛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing he was moved to Guizhou; before long he was demoted to Prefect of Aizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianqing he was moved to Guizhou, and before long demoted to Prefect of Aizhou.

sentences.zh: 遂良內憂禍，恐死不能自明，乃上表曰：「往者承乾廢，岑文本、劉洎奏東宮不可少曠，宜遣濮王居之，臣引義固爭。

translations.literal: Suiliang inwardly feared disaster and worried that in death he could not clear himself; he therefore submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly when Chengqian was deposed, Cen Wenben and Liu Ji memorialized that the Eastern Palace could not be left vacant long and that the Prince of Pu ought to be sent to dwell there; your subject cited principle and firmly contested this.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang inwardly feared disaster and worried that he could not clear his name even in death. He submitted a memorial saying, "When Chengqian was deposed, Cen Wenben and Liu Ji argued that the Eastern Palace could not be left vacant and that the Prince of Pu ought to dwell there. I firmly contested this on principle.

sentences.zh: 明日仗入，先帝留無忌、玄齡、勣及臣定策立陛下。

translations.literal: The next day, entering with the imperial guard, the late emperor kept Wuji, Xuanling, Ji, and your subject to settle the plan and install Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, entering with the imperial guard, the late emperor kept Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Li Ji, and me to settle the succession and install Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 當受遺詔。

translations.literal: At that time the testamentary edict was received.
translations.idiomatic: At that time we received the testamentary edict.

sentences.zh: 獨臣與無忌二人在，陛下方草土號慟，臣即奏請即位大行柩前。

translations.literal: Only your subject and Wuji were present; Your Majesty was then wailing in mourning dress, and your subject immediately memorialized requesting accession before the late emperor's bier.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wuji and I were present. Your Majesty was wailing in mourning dress, and I immediately memorialized requesting that you ascend the throne before the late emperor's bier.

sentences.zh: 當時陛下手抱臣頸，臣及無忌請即還京，發哀大告，內外寧謐。

translations.literal: At that time Your Majesty's hands embraced your subject's neck; your subject and Wuji requested an immediate return to the capital, the announcement of mourning and great proclamation, and inner and outer tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Your Majesty embraced my neck. Wuji and I urged an immediate return to the capital, the announcement of mourning, and the restoration of order within and without.

sentences.zh: 臣力小任重，動貽伊戚，螻螘餘齒，乞陛下哀憐。」

translations.literal: Your subject's strength is small yet his burden heavy; in action he constantly brings sorrow upon himself. An ant's remaining years beg Your Majesty's pity."
translations.idiomatic: My strength is small yet my burden heavy, and I constantly bring sorrow upon myself. In my remaining years I beg Your Majesty's pity.

sentences.zh: 帝昏懦，牽於武后，訖不省。

translations.literal: The emperor was dull and weak, pulled by Empress Wu, and to the end did not heed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was weak and muddled, pulled by Empress Wu, and to the end did not heed this.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he died, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 後二歲，許敬宗、李義府奏長孫無忌逆謀皆遂良驅煽，乃削官爵。

translations.literal: Two years later Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu memorialized that Zhangsun Wuji's treasonous plot was all incited by Suiliang; his offices and titles were then stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu memorialized that Zhangsun Wuji's treasonous plot had all been incited by Suiliang, and his offices and titles were stripped.

sentences.zh: 二子彥甫、彥沖流愛州，殺之。

translations.literal: His two sons Yanfu and Yancong were exiled to Aizhou and killed.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons Yanfu and Yancong were exiled to Aizhou and killed.

sentences.zh: 帝遣詔聽其家北還。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an edict permitting his family to return north.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict permitting his family to return north.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，復官爵。

translations.literal: During Shenlong his offices and titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era his offices and titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 德宗追贈太尉。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong posthumously granted him Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong posthumously granted him the title of Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 文宗時，詔以遂良五世孫虔為臨汝尉。

translations.literal: During Emperor Wenzong's time, an edict appointed Suiliang's fifth-generation descendant Qian as Captain of Linyou.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wenzong's reign, an edict appointed Suiliang's fifth-generation descendant Qian as Captain of Linyou.

sentences.zh: 安南觀察使高駢表遂良客窆愛州，二男一孫祔。

translations.literal: Annam Observation Commissioner Gao Pian memorialized that Suiliang was buried as a guest in Aizhou, with two sons and one grandson buried alongside.
translations.idiomatic: Annam Observation Commissioner Gao Pian reported that Suiliang had been buried in Aizhou, with two sons and one grandson buried alongside him.

sentences.zh: 咸通九年，詔訪其後護喪歸葬陽翟云。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xiantong an edict sought his descendants to escort the remains home for burial at Yangdi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Xiantong an edict sought his descendants to escort the remains home for burial at Yangdi.

sentences.zh: 曾 孫璆

translations.literal: Great-grandson: Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandson: Qiu.

sentences.zh: 遂良曾孫璆，字伯玉，擢進士第，累拜監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: Suiliang's great-grandson Qiu, style name Boyu, passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly appointed Acting Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang's great-grandson Qiu, whose style name was Boyu, passed the jinshi examination and rose to Acting Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 先天中，突厥圍北庭，詔璆持節監總督諸將，破之。

translations.literal: During Xiantian the Türks besieged Beiting; an edict ordered Qiu to bear the staff and supervise the overall command of the generals; he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiantian, when the Türks besieged Beiting, an edict ordered Qiu to bear the imperial staff and supervise the generals, and he defeated them.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史，拜禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor and appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attending Censor and appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 而氣象凝挺，不減在台時。

translations.literal: Yet his bearing was stern and upright, no less than when he was at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his bearing remained stern and upright, no less than when he served at the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 韓瑗，字伯玉，京兆三原人。

translations.literal: Han Yuan, style name Boyu, was a man of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yuan, whose style name was Boyu, was a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父仲良，武德初，與定律令，建言：「周律，其屬三千，秦、漢後約為五百。

translations.literal: His father Zhongliang, at the beginning of Wude, joined in codifying laws and statutes and submitted a proposal: "Under Zhou law there were three thousand articles; after Qin and Han they were reduced to about five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongliang, at the beginning of Wude, helped codify laws and statutes and proposed, "Under Zhou law there were three thousand articles; after Qin and Han they were reduced to about five hundred.

sentences.zh: 依古則繁，請崇寬簡，以示惟新。」

translations.literal: Following antiquity would make them cumbersome; I request honoring breadth and simplicity to show renewal."
translations.idiomatic: Following antiquity would make them cumbersome. I request honoring breadth and simplicity to show renewal.

sentences.zh: 於是采《開皇律》宜於時者定之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they selected from the Kaihuang Code what suited the times and fixed it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they selected from the Kaihuang Code what suited the times and fixed it.

sentences.zh: 終刑部尚書、秦州都督府長史、潁川縣公。

translations.literal: He ended as Minister of Justice, Chief Administrator of the Qinzhou Military Governor's Office, and Duke of Yingchuan County.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Minister of Justice, Chief Administrator of the Qinzhou Military Governor's Office, and Duke of Yingchuan County.

sentences.zh: 瑗少負節行。

translations.literal: Yuan from youth possessed integrity and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan from youth possessed integrity and strong moral character.

sentences.zh: 博學，曉吏事。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned and understood administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned and understood administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，以兵部侍郎襲爵。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he inherited the title as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he inherited the family title while serving as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年，遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghui he was transferred to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yonghui he was transferred to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 俄同中書門下三品，監修國史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he became Associate with the Three Departments at the rank of the Three Dukes and Supervisor of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he became Associate with the Three Departments at the rank of the Three Dukes and Supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 進侍中，兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Palace Attendant and concurrently Guest of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and concurrently Guest of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 王后之廢，瑗雪泣言曰：「皇后乃陛下在籓時先帝所娶，今無罪輒廢，非社稷計。」

translations.literal: When Empress Wang was to be deposed, Yuan wept as if in snow and said: "The empress was taken in marriage by the late emperor when Your Majesty was still a prince; now to depose her without crime is not a plan for the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wang was to be deposed, Yuan wept openly and said, "The empress was taken in marriage by the late emperor when Your Majesty was still a prince. To depose her without crime is not a plan for the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: This was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept this.

sentences.zh: 明日復諫曰：「王者立后，配天地，象日月。

translations.literal: The next day he remonstrated again: "When a king installs an empress, she matches Heaven and Earth and mirrors sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he remonstrated again, "When a king installs an empress, she matches Heaven and Earth and mirrors the sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 匹夫匹婦尚知相擇，況天子乎？

translations.literal: Even common men and women know to choose one another—how much more the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Even common men and women know to choose one another—how much more the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：『赫赫宗周，褒姒滅之。』

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'Splendid was the Zhou of the ancestors—Baosi destroyed it.'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, 'Splendid was the Zhou of the ancestors—Baosi destroyed it.'

sentences.zh: 臣讀至此，常輟卷太息，不圖本朝親見此禍。

translations.literal: When your subject reads to this point, he often puts down the scroll and sighs deeply—he never expected to witness this calamity in our own dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: When I read to this point, I often put down the scroll and sigh deeply. I never expected to witness this calamity in our own dynasty.

sentences.zh: 宗廟其不血食乎！」

translations.literal: Will the ancestral temples not go without blood sacrifice!"
translations.idiomatic: Will the ancestral temples not go without blood sacrifice!

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，詔引出。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered him led out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered him led out.

sentences.zh: 褚遂良貶潭州都督，明年瑗上言：「遂良受先帝顧託，一德無二，向日論事，至誠懇切，詎肯令陛下後堯、舜而塵史冊哉？

translations.literal: When Chu Suiliang was demoted to Military Governor of Tanzhou, the next year Yuan submitted a memorial: "Suiliang received the late emperor's testamentary charge, with one virtue and no second intent; in his daily discussions of affairs he was utterly sincere and earnest—how could he wish Your Majesty to fall behind Yao and Shun and stain the historical records?
translations.idiomatic: After Chu Suiliang was demoted to Military Governor of Tanzhou, Yuan submitted a memorial the next year: "Suiliang received the late emperor's testamentary charge with undivided loyalty. In his daily counsel he was utterly sincere—how could he wish Your Majesty to fall behind Yao and Shun and stain the historical records?

sentences.zh: 遭厚謗醜言，損陛下之明，折志士之銳。

translations.literal: He has suffered thick slander and ugly words, impairing Your Majesty's clarity and breaking the keen edge of men of resolve.
translations.idiomatic: He has suffered thick slander, impairing Your Majesty's clarity and breaking the keen edge of men of resolve.

sentences.zh: 況被遷以來，再離寒暑，其責塞矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, since his transfer he has passed through two cycles of cold and heat—his punishment is already sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since his transfer he has passed through two cycles of cold and heat—his punishment is already sufficient.

sentences.zh: 願寬無辜，以順眾心。」

translations.literal: I hope the innocent may be pardoned to accord with the people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: I hope the innocent may be pardoned to accord with the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「遂良之情，朕知之矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Suiliang's feelings—I know them already.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I know Suiliang's feelings already.

sentences.zh: 其孛戾好犯上，朕責之，詎有過邪？」

translations.literal: He is perverse and rebellious, fond of offending his superiors; I reprove him—is there any fault in that?"
translations.idiomatic: He is perverse and fond of offending his superiors. I reprove him—is there any fault in that?"

sentences.zh: 瑗曰：「遂良，社稷臣。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "Suiliang is a minister of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "Suiliang is a minister of the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 蒼蠅點白，傅致有罪。

translations.literal: A fly specks white and fabricates guilt.
translations.idiomatic: A fly can speck white and fabricate guilt.

sentences.zh: 昔微子既去，殷以亡；

translations.literal: Formerly, once Weizi departed, Yin perished;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, once Weizi departed, Yin perished;

sentences.zh: 張華不死，晉不及亂。

translations.literal: if Zhang Hua had not died, Jin would not have reached disorder.
translations.idiomatic: if Zhang Hua had not died, Jin would not have reached disorder.

sentences.zh: 陛下富有四海，安於清泰，忽驅逐舊臣，遂不省察乎？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty possesses the four seas and rests in clarity and peace—suddenly to drive away old ministers, will you not examine this?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty possesses the four seas and rests in peace—will you not examine why you suddenly drive away old ministers?

sentences.zh: 帝愈不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor listened even less.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor listened even less.

sentences.zh: 瑗憂憤，自表歸田里，不報。

translations.literal: Yuan, grieved and indignant, submitted a memorial requesting return to his fields; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: Grieved and indignant, Yuan submitted a memorial requesting retirement to his fields; no reply was given.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，許敬宗、李義府奏「瑗以桂州授遂良，桂用武地，倚之謀不軌。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu memorialized: "Yuan gave Guizhou to Suiliang; Gui is a military region, and relying on him he plotted rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianqing, Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu memorialized, "Yuan gave Guizhou to Suiliang. Gui is a military region, and relying on him they plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 於是貶振州刺史，逾年，卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was demoted to Prefect of Zhenzhou; after more than a year he died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was demoted to Prefect of Zhenzhou. After more than a year he died, aged fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌死，義府等復奏瑗與通謀，遣使即殺之；

translations.literal: When Zhangsun Wuji died, Yifu and others again memorialized that Yuan had conspired with him and sent envoys to kill him immediately;
translations.idiomatic: After Zhangsun Wuji died, Yifu and others again memorialized that Yuan had conspired with him and sent envoys to kill him immediately;

sentences.zh: 既至，瑗已死，發棺驗視乃還。

translations.literal: when they arrived Yuan was already dead; they opened the coffin to verify and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: when they arrived Yuan was already dead. They opened the coffin to verify and then returned.

sentences.zh: 追削官爵，籍其家，子孫謫廣州官奴。

translations.literal: His offices and titles were posthumously stripped, his household registered, and his descendants banished as official slaves in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His offices and titles were posthumously stripped, his household was registered, and his descendants were banished as official slaves in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，武后遺詔復官爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong Empress Wu's testamentary edict restored his offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shenlong, Empress Wu's testamentary edict restored his offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 自瑗與遂良相繼死，內外以言為讀將二十年。

translations.literal: From the time Yuan and Suiliang died in succession, within and without the court frank speech was taboo for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Yuan and Suiliang died in succession, frank speech was taboo at court and beyond for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 帝造奉天宮，御史李善感始上疏極言，時人喜之，謂為「鳳鳴朝陽」。

translations.literal: When the emperor built Fengtian Palace, Censor Li Shangan was the first to submit a memorial speaking to the utmost; people of the time rejoiced and called it "the phoenix crying toward the sun."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor built Fengtian Palace, Censor Li Shangan was the first to submit a bold memorial. People of the time rejoiced and called it "the phoenix crying toward the sun."

sentences.zh: 來濟，揚州江都人。

translations.literal: Lai Ji was a man of Jiangdu in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Ji was a native of Jiangdu in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父護兒，隋左翊衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Huer was Left Majestic Guard General of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huer was Left Majestic Guard General under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及難，闔門死之，濟幼得免。

translations.literal: During the disaster of Yuwen Huaji the whole household died; Ji, still young, escaped.
translations.idiomatic: During the disaster of Yuwen Huaji the whole household perished, but Ji, still young, escaped.

sentences.zh: 轉側流離，而篤志為文章，善議論，曉暢時務，擢進士。

translations.literal: Wandering and displaced, he yet devoted himself to writing, was skilled in discourse, understood current affairs clearly, and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Wandering and displaced, he devoted himself to writing, was skilled in discourse, understood current affairs clearly, and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累遷通事舍人。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he rose in succession to Attendant of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾敗，太宗問侍臣何以處之，莫敢對。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Chengqian failed, Taizong asked the attending ministers how to deal with him; none dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Chengqian failed, Taizong asked the attending ministers how to deal with him, but none dared reply.

sentences.zh: 濟曰：「陛下上不失為慈父，太子得盡天年，則善。」

translations.literal: Ji said: "Your Majesty above would not fail to be a loving father; if the crown prince is allowed to live out his natural years, that would be good."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Your Majesty would not fail to be a loving father. If the crown prince is allowed to live out his natural years, that would be best.

sentences.zh: 帝納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this.

sentences.zh: 除考功員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel's Merit Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel's Merit Office.

sentences.zh: 十八年，初置太子司議郎，高其選，而以濟為之，兼崇賢館直學士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Heir's Remonstrance Official was first established with high selection standards, and Ji was appointed to it, concurrently serving as Direct Academician of the Chongxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Heir's Remonstrance Official was first established with high selection standards, and Ji was appointed to it while also serving as Direct Academician of the Chongxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，拜中書侍郎，兼弘文館學士，監脩國史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Academician of the Hongwen Hall, and Supervisor of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonghui he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Academician of the Hongwen Hall, and Supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 俄同中書門下三品，封南陽縣男。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he became Associate with the Three Departments at the rank of the Three Dukes and was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he became Associate with the Three Departments at the rank of the Three Dukes and was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanyang County.

sentences.zh: 遷中書令，檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝將以武氏為后，濟諫曰：「王者立后，以承宗廟、母天下，宜擇禮義名家、幽閒令淑者，副四海之望，稱神祗之意。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to install Lady Wu as empress; Ji remonstrated: "When a king installs an empress, it is to inherit the ancestral temples and mother the realm; he ought to choose one from a ritually upright eminent clan, secluded, graceful, and virtuous, matching the hopes of the four seas and fulfilling the intent of the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to install Lady Wu as empress, Ji remonstrated, "A king installs an empress to inherit the ancestral temples and mother the realm. He ought to choose one from a ritually upright eminent clan—secluded, graceful, and virtuous—matching the hopes of the four seas and fulfilling the intent of the spirits.

sentences.zh: 故文王興姒，《關睢》之化，蒙被百姓，其福如彼；

translations.literal: Therefore King Wen raised the Si clan, and the transforming influence of "Guansui" covered the common people—such was its blessing;
translations.idiomatic: King Wen raised the Si clan, and the transforming influence of "Guansui" covered the common people—such was its blessing;

sentences.zh: 成帝縱欲，以婢為后，皇統中微，其禍如此。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng indulged his desires and made a maidservant empress; the imperial line declined midway—such was its calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng indulged his desires and made a maidservant empress; the imperial line declined midway—such was its calamity.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下詳察。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will examine this carefully."
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to examine this carefully.

sentences.zh: 初，武氏被寵，帝特號「宸妃」。

translations.literal: At first, when Lady Wu was favored, the emperor specially titled her "Imperial Consort."
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Lady Wu was favored, the emperor specially titled her Imperial Consort.

sentences.zh: 濟與韓瑗諫：「妃有常員，今別立號，不可。」

translations.literal: Ji and Han Yuan remonstrated: "Consorts have fixed quotas; to establish a separate title now cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Han Yuan remonstrated, "Consorts have fixed quotas. To establish a separate title now cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 武氏已立，不自安。

translations.literal: After Lady Wu was installed, she was not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After Lady Wu was installed as empress, she was not at ease.

sentences.zh: 后更謾言濟等忠鯁，恐前經執奏，輒懷反仄，請加賞慰，而實銜之。

translations.literal: The empress further spoke falsely that Ji and the others were loyal and blunt, fearing that because they had formerly submitted firm remonstrances they now harbored unease, and requested added rewards and consolation—yet in fact she resented them.
translations.idiomatic: The empress falsely praised Ji and the others as loyal and blunt, claiming they might harbor unease because of their earlier remonstrances, and requested rewards and consolation for them—yet in fact she resented them.

sentences.zh: 帝示濟及瑗，濟等益懼。

translations.literal: The emperor showed this to Ji and Yuan; Ji and the others grew even more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed this to Ji and Yuan, and they grew even more fearful.

sentences.zh: 顯慶初，兼太子賓客，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianqing he was concurrently Guest of the Heir and advanced in rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianqing he was concurrently Guest of the Heir and advanced in rank to Marquis.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗從容問馭下所宜，濟曰：「昔齊桓公出遊，見老人，命之食，曰：『請遺天下食。』

translations.literal: The emperor once casually asked what was fitting in governing subordinates; Ji said: "Formerly Duke Huan of Qi went on an outing, saw an old man, and ordered food for him; the man said: 'Please give food to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once casually asked what was fitting in governing subordinates. Ji said, "Formerly Duke Huan of Qi went on an outing, saw an old man, and ordered food for him. The man said, 'Please give food to the realm.

sentences.zh: 遺之衣，曰：『請遺天下衣。』

translations.literal: He gave him clothing, and the man said: 'Please give clothing to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him clothing, and the man said, 'Please give clothing to the realm.'

sentences.zh: 公曰：『吾府庫有限，安得而給？』

translations.literal: The duke said: 'My treasury is limited—how can I provide for all?
translations.idiomatic: The duke said, 'My treasury is limited—how can I provide for all?'

sentences.zh: 老人曰：『春不奪農時，即有食；

translations.literal: The old man said: 'If spring does not seize the farming season, there will be food;
translations.idiomatic: The old man said, 'If spring does not seize the farming season, there will be food;'

sentences.zh: 夏不奪蠶工，即有衣。』

translations.literal: if summer does not seize the silkworm workers, there will be clothing.
translations.idiomatic: if summer does not seize the silkworm workers, there will be clothing.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，省徭役，馭下之宜也。」

translations.literal: From this it is said: reducing corvée labor is what is fitting in governing subordinates."
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that reducing corvée labor is what is fitting in governing subordinates.'

sentences.zh: 于時山東役丁，歲別數萬人，又議取庸以償雇，紛然煩擾，故濟對及之。

translations.literal: At that time corvée laborers east of the mountains numbered tens of thousands each year, and there was further discussion of taking substitute payments to compensate hired labor—confusion and vexation abounded—therefore Ji answered with this.
translations.idiomatic: At that time corvée laborers east of the mountains numbered tens of thousands each year, and there was further discussion of substitute payments to compensate hired labor, causing widespread confusion—therefore Ji answered with this.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼詹事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was concurrently Steward of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was concurrently Steward of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 尋坐褚遂良事，貶台州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was implicated on account of Chu Suiliang's affair and demoted to Prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was implicated in Chu Suiliang's affair and demoted to Prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，徙庭州。

translations.literal: After a long time he was moved to Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was moved to Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，突厥入寇，濟總兵拒之，謂其眾曰：「吾嘗絓刑罔，蒙赦死，今當以身塞責。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo the Türks invaded; Ji gathered troops to resist them and said to his men: "I was once caught in the net of punishment and was spared death by pardon; now I must use my body to fulfill my duty."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longshuo the Türks invaded. Ji gathered troops to resist them and said to his men, "I was once caught in the net of punishment and was spared death by pardon. Now I must use my body to fulfill my duty.

sentences.zh: 遂不介胄而馳賊，沒焉，年五十三。

translations.literal: He then rode against the enemy without armor and perished, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode against the enemy without armor and perished, aged fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈楚州刺史，給靈轜還鄉。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Prefect of Chuzhou, and a funeral carriage was granted to return him home.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Prefect of Chuzhou, and a funeral carriage was granted to return him home.

sentences.zh: 初，濟與高智周、郝處俊、孫處約客宣城石仲覽家，仲覽衍於財，有器識，待四人甚厚。

translations.literal: At first Ji, together with Gao Zhizhou, Hao Chujun, and Sun Chuyue, lodged at the home of Shi Zhonglan of Xuancheng; Zhonglan was wealthy, had discernment, and treated the four men very generously.
translations.idiomatic: At first Ji lodged with Gao Zhizhou, Hao Chujun, and Sun Chuyue at the home of Shi Zhonglan of Xuancheng. Zhonglan was wealthy and discerning, and treated the four men very generously.

sentences.zh: 私相與言志，處俊曰：「願宰天下。」

translations.literal: In private they spoke to one another of their ambitions; Chujun said: "I wish to govern the realm."
translations.idiomatic: In private they spoke of their ambitions. Chujun said, "I wish to govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 濟及智周亦然。

translations.literal: Ji and Zhizhou said the same.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Zhizhou said the same.

sentences.zh: 處約曰：「宰相或不可冀，願為通事舍人足矣。」

translations.literal: Chuyue said: "Grand councilor may be beyond hope; to be an Attendant of Affairs would be enough."
translations.idiomatic: Chuyue said, "Grand councilor may be beyond hope. To be an Attendant of Affairs would be enough.

sentences.zh: 後濟領吏部，處約始以瀛州書佐入調，濟遽注曰「如志」，遂以處約為通事舍人。

translations.literal: Later, when Ji headed the Ministry of Personnel, Chuyue first entered for assignment as a clerical assistant from Yingzhou; Ji immediately noted "as wished" and thus appointed Chuyue Attendant of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Ji headed the Ministry of Personnel, Chuyue entered for assignment as a clerical assistant from Yingzhou. Ji immediately noted "as wished" and appointed Chuyue Attendant of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 後皆至公輔云。

translations.literal: "Later all reached the rank of grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Later all reached the rank of grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 異母兄 恒

translations.literal: Half-brother by different mother: Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Half-brother by different mother: Heng.

sentences.zh: 濟異母兄恒，上元中，為黃門侍郎、同中書門下三品，父本驍將，而恒、濟俱以學行稱，相次知政事。

translations.literal: Ji's half-brother Heng, during Shangyuan, was Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and Associate with the Three Departments at the rank of the Three Dukes; their father had originally been a fierce general, yet Heng and Ji were both known for learning and conduct and successively managed state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's half-brother Heng, during Shangyuan, was Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and Associate with the Three Departments at the rank of the Three Dukes. Their father had been a fierce general, yet Heng and Ji were both known for learning and conduct and successively managed state affairs.

sentences.zh: 時虞世南子昶無才術，曆將作少匠、工部侍郎，主工作。

translations.literal: At the time Yu Shinan's son Chang had no talent or skill; he successively served as Vice Director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings and Vice Director in the Ministry of Works, overseeing construction.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yu Shinan's son Chang had no talent or skill. He successively served as Vice Director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings and Vice Director in the Ministry of Works, overseeing construction.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗曰：「護兒兒作相，世南男作匠，文武豈有種邪？」

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong said: "Huer's son becomes chief minister, Shinan's son becomes a craftsman—can civil and military talent be inherited by breed?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong said, "Huer's son becomes chief minister, Shinan's son becomes a craftsman—can civil and military talent be inherited by breed?"

sentences.zh: 李義琰

translations.literal: Li Yiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiyan.

sentences.zh: 李義琰，魏州昌樂人，其先出隴西望姓。

translations.literal: Li Yiyan was a man of Changle in Weizhou; his ancestors came from the Wang clan of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiyan was a native of Changle in Weizhou. His ancestors came from the Wang clan of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，補太原尉。

translations.literal: Upon passing the jinshi examination he was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Upon passing the jinshi examination he was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 李勣為都督，僚吏憚其威，義琰獨敢廷辨曲直，勣甚禮之。

translations.literal: When Li Ji was military governor, his staff feared his authority; Yiyan alone dared argue right and wrong in open court, and Ji treated him with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ji was military governor, his staff feared his authority, but Yiyan alone dared argue right and wrong in open court, and Ji treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 徙白水令，有能名，擢司刑員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred as Magistrate of Baishui, gained a reputation for ability, and was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred as Magistrate of Baishui, gained a reputation for ability, and was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 義琰姿體魁秀，博學，有智識。

translations.literal: Yiyan's bearing was tall and distinguished; he was broadly learned and possessed wisdom and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyan was tall and distinguished in bearing, broadly learned, and possessed wisdom and discernment.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上元中，進同中書門下三品，兼太子右庶子。

translations.literal: During Shangyuan he was advanced to Associate with the Three Departments at the rank of the Three Dukes and concurrently Right Guardian of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: During Shangyuan he was advanced to Associate with the Three Departments at the rank of the Three Dukes and concurrently Right Guardian of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 高宗欲使武后攝國政，義琰與郝處俊固爭，事得寢。

translations.literal: Gaozong wished to have Empress Wu administer state affairs; Yiyan and Hao Chujun firmly contested this, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong wished to have Empress Wu administer state affairs, Yiyan and Hao Chujun firmly contested it, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 章懷太子之廢，盡赦宮臣罪，庶子薛元超等皆蹈舞，義琰獨引咎涕泣，搢紳義之。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Zhanghuai was deposed, all palace officials' crimes were pardoned; Guardians such as Xue Yuanchao all danced in joy, but Yiyan alone took blame upon himself and wept; the gentry honored him for this.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Zhanghuai was deposed, all palace officials' crimes were pardoned. Guardians such as Xue Yuanchao danced in joy, but Yiyan alone took blame upon himself and wept, and the gentry honored him for this.

sentences.zh: 帝每顧問，必鯁切不回。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor consulted him, he was always blunt and firm and did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor consulted him, he was always blunt and firm and did not yield.

sentences.zh: 宅無正寢，弟義璡為市堂材送之。

translations.literal: His residence had no proper main chamber; his younger brother Yijin purchased hall timber on the market and sent it to him.
translations.idiomatic: His residence had no proper main chamber. His younger brother Yijin purchased hall timber on the market and sent it to him.

sentences.zh: 義琰曰：「以吾為國相，且自愧，尚營美宇，是速吾禍，豈愛我者邪？」

translations.literal: Yiyan said: "That I am made chief minister of the state is already a source of shame to me; to still build a fine dwelling is to hasten my calamity—can this be love for me?"
translations.idiomatic: Yiyan said, "That I am made chief minister is already a source of shame to me. To still build a fine dwelling is to hasten my calamity—can this be love for me?

sentences.zh: 義璡曰：「凡仕為丞尉，且崇第舍，兄位高，安可逼下哉？」

translations.literal: Yijin said: "Even those who serve as assistant magistrates and captains still honor their residences; elder brother's rank is high—how can he be pressed down so low?"
translations.idiomatic: Yijin said, "Even those who serve as assistant magistrates and captains still honor their residences. Elder brother's rank is high—how can he be pressed so low?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「不然。

translations.literal: He answered: "That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "That is not so.

sentences.zh: 事難全遂，物不兩興。

translations.literal: Matters are hard to complete fully; things do not flourish in pairs.
translations.idiomatic: Matters are hard to complete fully; things do not flourish in pairs.

sentences.zh: 既處貴仕，又廣居宇，非有令德，必受其殃。」

translations.literal: To hold high office and also expand one's dwelling—without outstanding virtue, one will surely receive calamity."
translations.idiomatic: To hold high office and also expand one's dwelling—without outstanding virtue, one will surely receive calamity."

sentences.zh: 卒不許。

translations.literal: In the end he did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not consent.

sentences.zh: 後其木久腐，乃棄之。

translations.literal: Later the timber rotted over time, and it was discarded.
translations.idiomatic: Later the timber rotted and was discarded.

sentences.zh: 義琰改葬其先，使舅家移塋而兆其所。

translations.literal: Yiyan reburied his ancestors, making his maternal kin move their tombs so that he could establish his own burial site there.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyan reburied his ancestors, making his maternal kin move their tombs so that he could establish his own burial site there.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，怒曰：「是人不可使秉政。」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, he angrily said: "This man cannot be allowed to hold power."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, he angrily said, "This man cannot be allowed to hold power.

sentences.zh: 義琰懼，以疾乞骸骨，遷銀青光祿大夫，聽致仕，乃歸田裏。

translations.literal: Yiyan feared this, pleaded illness and requested retirement, was transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal, permitted to retire, and returned to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyan feared this, pleaded illness and requested retirement, was granted the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal, permitted to retire, and returned to his fields.

sentences.zh: 公卿以下悉祖餞通化門外，時人比漢疏廣。

translations.literal: From grand councilors down all saw him off with a farewell feast outside Tonghua Gate; people of the time compared him to Shu Guang of Han.
translations.idiomatic: From grand councilors down all saw him off with a farewell feast outside Tonghua Gate. People of the time compared him to Shu Guang of Han.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，起為懷州刺史，自以失武后意，辭不拜，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chuigong he was recalled as Prefect of Huaizhou; believing he had lost Empress Wu's favor, he declined the appointment and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chuigong he was recalled as Prefect of Huaizhou. Believing he had lost Empress Wu's favor, he declined the appointment and died.

sentences.zh: 子 巢

translations.literal: Son: Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Chao.

sentences.zh: 子巢，幼豪俊，善騎射，而不治細行。

translations.literal: His son Chao, from youth bold and talented, was skilled at mounted archery but did not attend to minor conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chao was bold and talented from youth, skilled at mounted archery, but did not attend to minor conduct.

sentences.zh: 義琰嘗拘之，絕其交遊。

translations.literal: Yiyan once confined him and cut off his associations.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyan once confined him and cut off his associations.

sentences.zh: 後亡走闕下，獻書陳利害。

translations.literal: Later he fled to the palace gates and submitted a memorial setting forth advantages and harms.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fled to the palace gates and submitted a memorial setting forth advantages and harms.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史，與李義府同按柳奭、韓瑗獄，遷殿中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor, together with Li Yifu investigated the cases of Liu Shi and Han Yuan, and was transferred to the Palace Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Investigating Censor, together with Li Yifu investigated the cases of Liu Shi and Han Yuan, and was transferred to the Palace Censorate.

sentences.zh: 上書忤旨，貶龍編主簿。

translations.literal: A memorial offended the imperial intent, and he was demoted to Registrar of Longbian.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial offended the imperial intent, and he was demoted to Registrar of Longbian.

sentences.zh: 從祖弟 義琛

translations.literal: Younger cousin by father's brother: Yichen.
translations.idiomatic: Younger cousin by father's brother: Yichen.

sentences.zh: 義琰從祖弟義琛。

translations.literal: Yiyan's younger cousin Yichen.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyan's younger cousin Yichen.

sentences.zh: 義琛擢進士第，曆監察御史。

translations.literal: Yichen passed the jinshi examination and successively served as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen passed the jinshi examination and successively served as Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，文成公主貢金，遇盜於岐州，主名不立。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, Princess Wencheng presented gold tribute; it encountered bandits at Qizhou, and the case could not be solved.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan, Princess Wencheng presented gold tribute. It was robbed at Qizhou, and the case could not be solved.

sentences.zh: 太宗召群御史至，目義琛曰：「是人神情爽拔，可使推捕。」

translations.literal: Taizong summoned the censors and, looking at Yichen, said: "This man's spirit is bright and outstanding; he can be sent to investigate and capture them."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned the censors and, looking at Yichen, said, "This man's spirit is bright and outstanding. He can be sent to investigate and capture them.

sentences.zh: 義琛往，數日獲賊。

translations.literal: Yichen went, and within several days captured the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen went, and within several days captured the bandits.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，為加七階。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and promoted him seven ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and promoted him seven ranks.

sentences.zh: 初，義琰使高麗，其王據榻召見，義琰不拜，曰：「吾，天子使，可當小國之君，奈何倨見我？」

translations.literal: At first, when Yiyan was envoy to Goguryeo, its king summoned him while reclining on a couch; Yiyan did not bow and said: "I am the Son of Heaven's envoy, equal to the ruler of a small state—why receive me with such arrogance?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yiyan was envoy to Goguryeo, its king summoned him while reclining on a couch. Yiyan did not bow and said, "I am the Son of Heaven's envoy, equal to the ruler of a small state—why receive me with such arrogance?

sentences.zh: 王祠屈，為加禮。

translations.literal: The king apologized and showed him added courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The king apologized and showed him added courtesy.

sentences.zh: 及義琛再使，亦坐召之，義琛匍匐拜伏。

translations.literal: When Yichen went as envoy a second time, he too was summoned while seated, and Yichen crawled and prostrated himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Yichen went as envoy a second time, he too was summoned while seated, and Yichen crawled and prostrated himself.

sentences.zh: 時人由是見兄弟優劣。

translations.literal: People of the time thus saw the brothers' relative merits.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time thus saw the brothers' relative merits.

sentences.zh: 累遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 為雍州長史，時關輔大饑，詔貧人就食商、鄧，義琛恐流徙不還，上疏固爭。

translations.literal: As Chief Administrator of Yongzhou, when the Guanzhong region suffered great famine, an edict ordered the poor to go for food to Shang and Deng; Yichen feared they would drift away and not return, and submitted a memorial firmly contesting this.
translations.idiomatic: As Chief Administrator of Yongzhou, when the Guanzhong region suffered great famine, an edict ordered the poor to go for food to Shang and Deng. Yichen feared they would drift away and not return, and submitted a memorial firmly contesting this.

sentences.zh: 左遷黎州都督，終岐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was demoted and transferred as Military Governor of Lizhou and ended as Prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Military Governor of Lizhou and ended his career as Prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 子綰，為柏人令，有仁政，縣為立祠。

translations.literal: His son Wan served as Magistrate of Bairen, had benevolent governance, and the county erected a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wan served as Magistrate of Bairen with benevolent governance, and the county erected a shrine for him.

sentences.zh: 上官儀，字遊韶，陝州陝人。

translations.literal: Shangguan Yi had the courtesy name Youshao and was a native of Shan in Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Yi had the courtesy name Youshao and was a native of Shan in Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父弘，為隋江都宮副監，大業末，為陳棱所殺。

translations.literal: His father Hong served under Sui as vice supervisor of Jiangdu Palace; at the end of Daye, he was killed by Chen Leng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hong served under Sui as vice supervisor of Jiangdu Palace; at the end of Daye, he was killed by Chen Leng.

sentences.zh: 時儀幼，左右匿免，冒為沙門服。

translations.literal: Yi was young at the time, and attendants hid him so that he escaped, disguising him in Buddhist monk’s clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was young at the time, and attendants hid him so that he escaped, disguising him in Buddhist monk’s clothing.

sentences.zh: 浸工文詞，涉貫墳典。

translations.literal: Gradually he became skilled in literary writing and ranged through the classics and ancient texts.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually he became skilled in literary writing and ranged through the classics and ancient texts.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，擢進士第，召授弘文館直學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, he was selected in the jinshi examination and summoned to be appointed duty scholar of the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan, he was selected in the jinshi examination and summoned to be appointed duty scholar of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Secretary in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretary in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 太宗每屬文，遣儀視槁，宴私未嘗不預。

translations.literal: Whenever Taizong composed writings, he sent for Yi to review the drafts, and Yi was always included in private banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Taizong composed writings, he sent for Yi to review the drafts, and Yi was always included in private banquets.

sentences.zh: 轉起居郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Court Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Court Diarist.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，為秘書少監，進西台同東西台三品，時以雍州司士參軍韋絢為殿中侍御史，或疑非遷。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, Yi became vice supervisor of the Palace Library and was advanced to Xitai Tong Dong-Xitai Sanpin. At the time, Wei Xuan, judicial staff officer of Yongzhou, was made palace attendant censor, and some doubted that this was a promotion.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne, Yi became vice supervisor of the Palace Library and was advanced to Xitai Tong Dong-Xitai Sanpin. At the time, Wei Xuan, judicial staff officer of Yongzhou, was made palace attendant censor, and some doubted that this was a promotion.

sentences.zh: 儀曰：「此野人語耳。御史供奉赤墀下，接武夔龍，簉羽鵷鷺，豈雍州判佐比乎？」

translations.literal: Yi said, “This is only rustic talk. A censor serves below the red steps, treads alongside Kui and Long, and ranks among the plumed ranks of yuanyang and egret officials. How can that compare with an assistant adjudicating official in Yongzhou?”
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, “This is only rustic talk. A censor serves below the red steps, treads alongside Kui and Long, and ranks among the plumed ranks of yuanyang and egret officials. How can that compare with an assistant adjudicating official in Yongzhou?”

sentences.zh: 時以為清言。

translations.literal: People of the time considered this refined discourse.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time considered this refined discourse.

sentences.zh: 儀工詩，其詞綺錯婉媚。

translations.literal: Yi was skilled at poetry; his language was ornate, interwoven, graceful, and charming.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was skilled at poetry; his language was ornate, interwoven, graceful, and charming.

sentences.zh: 及貴顯，人多效之，謂為「上官體」。

translations.literal: When he became eminent, many people imitated him, calling it the “Shangguan style.”
translations.idiomatic: When he became eminent, many people imitated him, calling it the “Shangguan style.”

sentences.zh: 麟德元年，坐梁王忠事下獄死，籍其家。

translations.literal: In Linde 1, he was implicated in the affair of Prince Zhong of Liang, sent to prison, and died; his household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In Linde 1, he was implicated in the affair of Prince Zhong of Liang, sent to prison, and died; his household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 初，武后得志，遂牽制帝，專威福，帝不能堪；又引道士行厭勝，中人王伏勝發之。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Empress Wu gained her will, she constrained the emperor and monopolized authority over punishments and favors, which the emperor could not endure. She also brought in Daoists to perform apotropaic rites, and the eunuch Wang Fusheng exposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Empress Wu gained her will, she constrained the emperor and monopolized authority over punishments and favors, which the emperor could not endure. She also brought in Daoists to perform apotropaic rites, and the eunuch Wang Fusheng exposed it.

sentences.zh: 帝因大怒，將廢為庶人，召儀與議。

translations.literal: The emperor was therefore furious and intended to depose her to commoner status, summoning Yi to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was therefore furious and intended to depose her to commoner status, summoning Yi to discuss it.

sentences.zh: 儀曰：「皇后專恣，海內失望，宜廢之以順人心。」

translations.literal: Yi said, “The empress is autocratic and willful, and all within the seas have lost hope. She should be deposed in order to accord with the people’s hearts.”
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, “The empress is autocratic and willful, and all within the seas have lost hope. She should be deposed in order to accord with the people’s hearts.”

sentences.zh: 帝使草詔。

translations.literal: The emperor had him draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 左右奔告後，後自申訴，帝乃悔；

translations.literal: Attendants ran to inform the empress, and the empress came herself to plead her case, whereupon the emperor regretted it.
