translations.idiomatic: Attendants ran to inform the empress, and the empress came herself to plead her case, whereupon the emperor regretted it.

sentences.zh: 又恐後怨恚，乃曰：「上官儀教我。」

translations.literal: He also feared the empress’s resentment, and so said, “Shangguan Yi instructed me to do it.”
translations.idiomatic: He also feared the empress’s resentment, and so said, “Shangguan Yi instructed me to do it.”

sentences.zh: 後由是深惡儀。

translations.literal: Because of this, the empress deeply hated Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, the empress deeply hated Yi.

sentences.zh: 始，忠為陳王時，儀為諮議，與王伏勝同府。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhong was Prince of Chen, Yi had served as advisory official, in the same office as Wang Fusheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhong was Prince of Chen, Yi had served as advisory official, in the same office as Wang Fusheng.

sentences.zh: 至是，許敬宗構儀與忠謀大逆，後志也。

translations.literal: At this point, Xu Jingzong framed Yi as having plotted great treason with Zhong; this was the empress’s intention.
translations.idiomatic: At this point, Xu Jingzong framed Yi as having plotted great treason with Zhong; this was the empress’s intention.

sentences.zh: 自褚遂良等元老大臣相次屠履，公卿莫敢正議，獨儀納忠，禍又不旋踵，由是天下之政歸於後，而帝拱手矣。

translations.literal: From the time old and senior ministers such as Chu Suiliang were slaughtered one after another, the dukes and high ministers did not dare make correct arguments. Yi alone accepted Zhong’s case, and disaster followed at once. From this, the governance of the realm returned to the empress, while the emperor folded his hands.
translations.idiomatic: From the time old and senior ministers such as Chu Suiliang were slaughtered one after another, the dukes and high ministers did not dare make correct arguments. Yi alone accepted Zhong’s case, and disaster followed at once. From this, the governance of the realm returned to the empress, while the emperor folded his hands.

sentences.zh: 子庭芝，歷周王府屬，亦被殺。

translations.literal: His son Tingzhi successively served as an official of the Prince of Zhou's household and was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tingzhi served as an official of the Prince of Zhou's household and was also killed.

sentences.zh: 庭芝女，中宗時為昭容，追贈儀為中書令、秦州都督、楚國公；

translations.literal: Tingzhi's daughter, during Zhongzong's time a Lady of Bright Countenance, posthumously granted Yi the titles of Director of the Secretariat, Military Governor of Qinzhou, and Duke of Chu;
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi's daughter, who during Zhongzong's reign was a Lady of Bright Countenance, had Yi posthumously granted the titles of Director of the Secretariat, Military Governor of Qinzhou, and Duke of Chu;

sentences.zh: 庭芝黃門侍郎、岐州刺史、天水郡公，以禮改葬。

translations.literal: Tingzhi was made Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, Prefect of Qizhou, and Duke of Tianshui Commandery, and was reburied according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi was made Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, Prefect of Qizhou, and Duke of Tianshui Commandery, and was reburied according to ritual.

translations.literal: Eulogium.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：高宗之不君，可與為治邪？

translations.literal: The eulogium says: Gaozong was no true ruler—how could one govern with him?
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Gaozong was no true ruler—how could one govern with him?

sentences.zh: 內牽嬖陰，外劫讒言，以無忌之親，遂良之忠，皆顧命大臣，一旦誅斥，忍而不省。

translations.literal: Inwardly pulled by the shadow of a favorite, outwardly seized by slanderous words—Wuji, his closest kin, and Suiliang, his loyal minister, both testamentary grand ministers, were in one day executed and cast out, and he endured this without reflection.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly pulled by a favorite's shadow, outwardly seized by slanderous words—Wuji, his closest kin, and Suiliang, his loyal minister, both testamentary grand ministers, were in one day executed and cast out, and he endured this without reflection.

sentences.zh: 反天之剛，撓陽之明，卒使牝咮鳴辰，祚移后家，可不哀哉！

translations.literal: He reversed Heaven's firmness and bent the brightness of the yang; in the end he let the hen crow at dawn and the throne pass to the empress's house—how pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: He reversed Heaven's firmness and bent the brightness of the yang; in the end he let the hen crow at dawn and the throne pass to the empress's house—how pitiable!

sentences.zh: 天以女戎間唐而興，雖義士仁人抗之以死，決不可支。

translations.literal: Heaven used the female warrior to divide Tang and rise; though men of righteousness and benevolence resisted with their lives, it could decisively not be sustained.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven used the female warrior to divide Tang and rise. Though men of righteousness resisted with their lives, the dynasty could not be sustained.

sentences.zh: 然瑗、濟、義琰、儀四子可謂知所守矣。

translations.literal: Yet Yuan, Ji, Yiyan, and Yi—the four of them—can be said to have known what to hold to.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yuan, Ji, Yiyan, and Yi—the four of them—can be said to have known what to hold to.

sentences.zh: 噫，使長孫不逐江夏、害吳王，褚不譖死劉洎，其盛德可少訾乎！

translations.literal: Alas! If Zhangsun had not driven away Jiangxia and harmed Prince Wu, and if Chu had not slandered Liu Ji to his death, could their great virtue have been slightly faulted?
translations.idiomatic: Alas! If Zhangsun had not driven away Jiangxia and harmed Prince Wu, and if Chu had not slandered Liu Ji to his death, could their great virtue have been even slightly faulted?
